docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Every dox command, with its options and the files it writes.

The commands come from packages/dox-cli/lib/src/command_registry.dart. The file templates are Dart strings inside packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/. The path of each template is given below.

How to install the CLI is on the Dox CLI page.

Rules that apply to every command:

  • dox with no command prints Could not find a command. Rundox helpfor more information.
  • An unknown command prints Could not find a command named "<name>".
  • Too few or too many arguments prints Invalid number of arguments for command "<name>". with the expected count.
  • A name you pass is turned into snake_case for the file and PascalCase for the class. BlogPost and blog_post give the same result.
  • Every make:* command also answers to its create:* name, like create:model. dox help <command> shows the aliases.
  • A make:* command does not overwrite. When the file exists it prints <name> already exists and stops.

docs.title: dox create
docs.text:
dox create <project_name> [--version <version>]

Makes a new project from the dox-sample repo.

Option Meaning --version <v> (or --v) The release tag to clone, like 3.0.0-alpha.5 or v3.0.0-alpha.5. Without it, the newest dox-sample release with the same major version as the CLI is used (pre-releases included).

What it does:

  1. Turns the name into snake_case. Stops with Folder name "<name>" already exist when the folder is there.
  2. Picks the release (see --version above) from the release list of dartondox/dox-sample.
  3. Runs git clone --depth 1 --branch v<version> https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample.git <name>.
  4. Deletes the .git folder.
  5. Replaces dox_sample with your project name in every file, except files under bin/dox.
  6. Copies .env.example to .env and writes a new random APP_KEY to it, like dox key:generate. It skips this step when .env is already there.

Needs curl and git on the PATH.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_project.dart.

docs.title: dox serve
docs.text:
dox serve [--ignore-build-runner]
dox s
dox server

Starts the dev server.

Option Meaning --ignore-build-runner Do not start dart run build_runner watch.

What it does:

  1. Starts dart run build_runner watch (unless the option is set).
  2. Starts dart run bin/server.dart and prints its output.
  3. Watches the project folder. When a .dart file changes it prints [Dox] File changed: <file>, waits 500 ms, kills the server and starts it again.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart.

docs.title: dox build
docs.text:
dox build

AOT compiles the app for production into build/bundle. Use this in production, not dart run.

What it does:

  1. When pubspec.yaml contains build_runner: runs dart run build_runner build. Stops with exit code 1 when it fails.
  2. Runs dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build.
  3. Copies db/ to build/bundle/db (migrations are read at start).
  4. Copies .env.example to build/bundle/.env.example.
  5. Prints [Dox] Built build/bundle. Run it with: cd build/bundle && ./bin/server.

Output:

Path What build/bundle/bin/server the native binary, no Dart SDK needed build/bundle/lib/ native libraries from build hooks (SQLite, dox_http_native, ...) build/bundle/db/ your migrations build/bundle/.env.example copy it to .env or set real env vars

dart compile exe can not build packages with build hooks, so the CLI uses dart build cli.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart (buildServer).

docs.title: dox build_runner:build and dox build_runner:watch
docs.text:
dox build_runner:build
dox build_runner:watch

Run dart run build_runner build once, or dart run build_runner watch. No options. The CLI does not pass --delete-conflicting-outputs (build_runner removed that flag).

docs.title: dox key:generate
docs.text:
dox key:generate

Makes a 32 character key (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, from Random.secure()) and writes it to APP_KEY in .env. Prints <key> : Key have been updated successfully in .env!.

What it does with .env:

  • Reads .env in the current folder. The file must exist, else the command fails with a file error.
  • Replaces the value of APP_KEY. Every other line stays as it is, in the same order. This keeps comments, blank lines, quotes and values with more than one = (like DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?a=b).
  • Adds APP_KEY=<key> as the first line when there is no APP_KEY.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/generate_key.dart.

docs.title: dox env:generate
docs.text:
dox env:generate

Writes lib/config/env.dart, the typed env class, from .env.example.

  • Stops with .env.example is missing. (exit code 1) when there is no example file.
  • Stops with lib/config/env.dart is already there. Delete it to make it again. (exit code 1) when the file exists.
  • Prints Rundart run build_runner buildto make env.g.dart. when done.

Rules for each key: digits give int get x => <value>;, true/false give bool, an empty value gives String? get x;, any other value gives String get x; (required, no default). # comment lines above a key become its doc comment. A key that does not map back from camelCase gets @EnvKey('KEY').

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart (EnvScaffold).

docs.title: dox env:check
docs.text:
dox env:check

Loads AppEnv from lib/config/env.dart with the real environment and .env. Prints The env is valid. or an EnvException with every missing or bad key (exit code 1).

It writes a small script to .dart_tool/dox/env_check.dart and runs it with dart run. It needs lib/config/env.dart and a name: in pubspec.yaml.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart (envCheck).

docs.title: dox openapi:generate
docs.text:
dox openapi:generate [dir]

Runs dart run bin/openapi.dart [dir]. That file writes openapi.json and openapi.yaml into dir (default storage/openapi). Stops with bin/openapi.dart is missing. (exit code 1) when the file is not there. See OpenAPI.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/openapi_generate.dart.

docs.title: dox update
docs.text:
dox update

Installs the newest CLI with the same major version as the one you have. Pre-releases count. It reads the version list from pub.dev, then runs dart pub global activate dox <version>.

Source: packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/update_dox.dart.

docs.title: dox version
docs.text:
dox version
dox v
dox -v
dox --version

Prints Dox version: <version>. Aliases: --version, -version, v, -v, --v.

docs.title: dox help
docs.text:
dox help [command]

Without a command: lists every command by category. With a command: prints its usage, description, category, aliases and argument count.

docs.title: dox make:controller
docs.text:
dox make:controller <name> [-r]

Alias: create:controller. The other make:* commands below have the same kind of alias.

Option Meaning -r A resource controller with index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy.

A trailing Controller in the name is removed: UserController and User give the same file.

Form Writes Template plain lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_controller.dart -r lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart _getResourceSample in the same file

The class has @Inject(), so the container makes it. A comment shows the route to add, like Route.get<BlogController>('path', (BlogController c) => c.index);. After the file is made, the CLI tells you to run dart run build_runner build. That adds the controller to lib/container.g.dart.

docs.title: dox make:middleware
docs.text:
dox make:middleware <name>

Writes lib/app/http/middleware/<name>.middleware.dart: a class <Name>Middleware extends IDoxMiddleware with a handle(IDoxRequest req) that returns req. A trailing Middleware in the name is removed.

Template: _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_middleware.dart.

docs.title: dox make:dto
docs.text:
dox make:dto <name>

Writes lib/app/http/dtos/<name>.dto.dart: a @Dto() class with one name field and part '<name>.dto.g.dart';. A trailing Dto in the name is removed. Prints Rundox build_runner:buildto make <name>.dto.g.dart.

Template: _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_dto.dart.

docs.title: dox make:serializer
docs.text:
dox make:serializer <name>

Writes lib/app/http/serializers/<name>.serializer.dart: a class <Name>Serializer extends Serializer<<Name>>. It imports the model from lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart. A trailing Serializer in the name is removed.

Template: _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_serializer.dart.

docs.title: dox make:model
docs.text:
dox make:model <name> [-m|--migration]
dox create:model <name> [-m|--migration]

Writes lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart: a @DoxModel() class with part '<name>.model.g.dart';.

Option Meaning -m or --migration Also make a create_<table>_table migration. The table is the plural snake name: BlogPost gives blog_posts. The model then gets @DoxModel(table: 'blog_posts').

Any other second argument prints Invalid option <x>, use -m or --migration (exit code 1).

Template: _getSample in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_model.dart.

docs.title: dox make:migration
docs.text:
dox make:migration <name> [--sql]
dox create:migration <name> [--sql]
Option Meaning --sql Make a .sql file with -- up and -- down sections instead of a Dart class.

Writes db/migration/<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<hhmmss>_<name>.dart (or .sql). Characters that are not letters, digits or _ are removed from the name.

For a Dart migration it also:

  • writes db/migration/migrations.dart, the registry of every Dart migration in the folder, sorted by name;
  • writes bin/migrate.dart when it is missing, and prints bin/migrate.dart created.

The Dart template depends on the name:

Name up() down() create_<table>_table schema.create('<table>', ...) with id() and timestamps() schema.dropIfExists('<table>') <x>_to_<table>_table (also from, in, on) schema.table('<table>', ...) schema.table('<table>', ...) anything else a comment a comment

Templates: dartMigrationSource, migrateEntrySource and _sampleSql in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_migration.dart.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
All migration:* commands work the same way:

  1. When bin/migrate.dart exists: write the registry again, then run dart run bin/migrate.dart <command> [args]. Your app code runs, so Dart migrations work.
  2. When there is no bin/migrate.dart but db/migration has Dart files: print db/migration has Dart migrations, but bin/migrate.dart is missing. (exit code 1).
  3. Else: run the .sql migrations with Migrator() from dox_migration in the CLI process.

The database comes from DB_CONNECTION, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD and DB_DATABASE (or DB_NAME). See Environment variables. A failed run prints the error and sets exit code 1.

Command Aliases What it does dox migration:run dox migrate Run the migrations that did not run yet. dox migration:rollback [--step=<count>] dox migrate:rollback Undo the last batch, or the last <count> migrations. Any other option prints Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count> (exit code 1). dox migration:reset dox migrate:reset Undo every migration. dox migration:refresh dox migrate:refresh Undo every migration, then run them all again. dox migration:fresh dox migrate:fresh Drop every table, then run all migrations. dox migration:status dox migrate:status Print which migrations ran, and their batch.

--seed after migration:run, migration:refresh or migration:fresh runs dox db:seed when the migrations end well.

docs.title: Factories and seeders
docs.text:
Command Aliases What it does dox make:factory <model> dox create:factory Make db/factories/<model>.factory.dart. It imports the model with the package name of pubspec.yaml. dox make:seeder <name> dox create:seeder Make db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart. It writes db/seeders/seeders.dart again, and makes bin/seed.dart when it is missing. dox db:seed [--class=<name>] Write db/seeders/seeders.dart again, then run dart run bin/seed.dart. Default seeder: DatabaseSeeder.

Templates: createFactory in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_factory.dart, and createSeeder and seedEntrySource in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_seeder.dart.

docs.title: Queue
docs.text:
These commands run the app script bin/queue.dart with dart run. The script comes from the dox_queue package. dox make:job makes it when it is missing. Input, output and errors go straight to your terminal. Ctrl+C (SIGINT) and SIGTERM are sent on to the script, so a worker can finish its job and stop. The exit code of the script is the exit code of dox. When bin/queue.dart is missing, the command prints how to set it up and exits with code 1.

Command Runs What it does dox make:job <name> Make lib/app/jobs/<name>.job.dart with a @Job() class that extends DoxJob. Make bin/queue.dart when it is missing. Print a hint to add dox_queue to pubspec.yaml and to run dox build_runner:build. dox queue:work [flags] bin/queue.dart work [flags] Run the worker. dox queue:failed bin/queue.dart failed List the failed jobs. dox queue:retry <id\|all> bin/queue.dart retry <id\|all> Put one failed job, or all of them, back on the queue. dox queue:forget <id> bin/queue.dart forget <id> Delete one failed job. dox queue:flush bin/queue.dart flush Delete all failed jobs.

Flags of queue:work, passed on as they are:

Flag Meaning --queue=a,b The queues to read, in this order. --concurrency=N How many jobs run at the same time. --once Run one job, then stop. --tries=N How many times a job may run before it is marked as failed. --timeout=S Seconds a job may run. --sleep=S Seconds to wait when the queue is empty. --stop-when-empty Stop when the queue is empty.

The bin/queue.dart that make:job writes (<app> is the name in pubspec.yaml):

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';
import 'package:<app>/jobs.g.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await QueueWorker(jobs: jobRegistry, app: appConfig).run(args);
}

Templates: createJob and queueEntrySource in packages/dox-cli/lib/src/tools/create_job.dart.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
These commands run the app script bin/schedule.dart with dart run. They pass the signals, the terminal and the exit code the same way as the queue commands. When bin/schedule.dart is missing, the command prints how to set it up and exits with code 1.

Command Runs What it does dox schedule:work bin/schedule.dart work Run the scheduler and keep it running. dox schedule:run bin/schedule.dart run Run the tasks that are due now, once. dox schedule:list bin/schedule.dart list List the scheduled tasks. dox schedule:test <name> bin/schedule.dart test <name> Run one task now.

To set it up, add dox_scheduler to pubspec.yaml, then make two small files. The exact names come from the dox_scheduler package. This is the shape:

// lib/config/schedule.dart
import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';

final Schedule schedule = Schedule()
  ..call('report', () async {/* your task */}).dailyAt('02:00');

// bin/schedule.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/schedule.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await SchedulerRunner(
    schedule: schedule,
    app: appConfig,
    config: scheduleConfig,
  ).run(args);
}

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Every env var the framework and its packages read.

How to read your own keys with the typed env class is on the Environment Variables page.

The code reads env vars in three ways:

  • Env.get() and EnvReader (dox_core): a real environment variable wins over the .env file.
  • Platform.environment straight: only the real environment, .env is not read.
  • dox_migration has its own loadEnv(): it reads .env and the real environment. A real environment variable wins, the same as Env.get().

docs.title: Read by the framework
docs.text: Variable Who reads it Default Meaning Example APP_ENV dox_core (Dox().checkAppKey(), OpenApiConfig.isEnabled) empty Any value except development, local or test (also empty) makes a bad APP_KEY a startup error: missing, not exactly 32 characters, or a public sample key. In development, local and test it is only a warning. development or local turn the /docs routes on when openApi.enabled is null. Read with Env.get. APP_ENV=production PORT dox_core (DoxServer.portFor()) not set The port to listen on, when APP_PORT is not set. Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it. APP_PORT wins when both are set. Read with Env.get. PORT=8080 APP_HOST dox_core (DoxServer.hostFor()) not set (all interfaces, ::) The host to listen on. 127.0.0.1 keeps the app off the network, for an app behind a proxy on the same machine. AppConfig.host wins over it. Read with Env.get. APP_HOST=127.0.0.1 DOX_HTTP_THREAD dox_http_native (Rust, shared_thread()) not set (one thread per isolate) shared puts the servers of all isolates on one network thread. Off by default: on 2 cores it cut req/s by a quarter. Real environment only (std::env::var), not .env. DOX_HTTP_THREAD=shared DATABASE_URL dox_orm (DatabaseConfig.url), dox_migration not set A database url. When it is set, it wins over DB_CONNECTION and the other DB_* keys. dox_orm reads it from the real environment only. See Database url. DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:secret@db:5432/blog?sslmode=require DB_CONNECTION dox_migration (DbConnection.config()) postgres postgres, mysql or sqlite. Any other value means postgres. DB_CONNECTION=sqlite DB_HOST dox_migration localhost Database host. A path that starts with / is a Unix socket: the folder for Postgres, the socket file for MySQL. DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT dox_migration 5432 (postgres), 3306 (mysql) Database port. DB_PORT=5432 DB_USERNAME dox_migration postgres (postgres), root (mysql) Database user. DB_USERNAME=app DB_PASSWORD dox_migration postgres (postgres), empty (mysql) Database password. DB_PASSWORD=secret DB_DATABASE dox_migration falls back to DB_NAME, then dox Database name. For sqlite: the file path. DB_DATABASE=dox DB_NAME dox_migration dox Same as DB_DATABASE. DB_DATABASE wins when both are set. DB_NAME=dox HOME / USERPROFILE build hooks of dox_http_native, dox_postgres_native, dox_mysql_native empty Used to find ~/.cargo/bin/cargo when the library must be built from source. set by the OS DART_VM_OPTIONS the Dart VM not set Flags for the VM. The AOT binary from dox build reads it. Dox never sets VM flags for you. See Performance. DART_VM_OPTIONS=--new_gen_semi_max_size=64

docs.title: Read by a new project
docs.text:
A new project (dox create) reads these keys through its typed env class, lib/config/env.dart. The framework itself does not read them. In code, use the getter: env.appPort.

Variable Getter Type Default Used for APP_NAME appName String dox LoggerConfig.name. APP_ENV appEnv String development development, staging or production. env.isDevelopment is true for development. It turns on prettyPrint of the logger and the query log of the database. Also read by the framework (see above). APP_PORT appPort int 3000 AppConfig.serverPort. When APP_PORT is not set, Dox listens on PORT if the env has it. APP_KEY appKey String required AppConfig.appKey. It must be exactly 32 characters. Run dox key:generate for one. The app stops at start when it is missing, has another length, or is a public sample key (only a warning in development, local and test). APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE appTotalIsolate int? not set: one per CPU core AppConfig.totalIsolate. LOG_LEVEL logLevel String info LoggerConfig.level. CACHE_STORE cacheStore String file CacheConfig.defaultStore: memory, file or redis. STORAGE_DISK storageDisk String local StorageConfig.defaultDisk: local, s3 or memory. DB_CONNECTION dbConnection String sqlite DatabaseConfig.connection: sqlite, postgres or mysql. DB_NAME dbName String db/dox.sqlite The database name. For SQLite: the file path. DB_HOST dbHost String localhost Database host. DB_PORT dbPort int? not set: 5432 for Postgres, 3306 for MySQL Database port. DB_USERNAME dbUsername String postgres Database user. DB_PASSWORD dbPassword String empty Database password.

To add a key, add a getter to AppEnv and run dart run build_runner build. See Environments.

The .env.example of a new project:

.env.example
APP_NAME=dox
APP_ENV=development
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=

CACHE_STORE=file
STORAGE_DISK=local

# SQLite needs no setup. The file is created at the first start.
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

# Postgres or MySQL: set DB_CONNECTION=postgres or mysql and fill these in.
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres

docs.title: How .env is parsed
docs.text:
Env.parse() in packages/dox-core/lib/env/env.dart:

  • One KEY=value per line. The key is trimmed. A line that starts with # is a comment.
  • The value is everything after the first =. A second = is kept.
  • # after a space starts a comment: KEY=abc # note gives abc. KEY=abc#def stays abc#def.
  • A value in quotes (", ' or `) is kept as it is, also a #. The quotes are removed.
  • An empty value, or the text null, counts as missing.
  • The file is read once per isolate, from the current working directory.

dox_migration has its own simpler parser. It removes every quote character and does not strip # note comments. Keep comments on their own line.

docs.title: Error index
docs.text:
A lookup table of the messages Dox prints or throws. Search this page for the text you see.

  • <...> is a part that changes, like a name or a number.
  • Dart adds a prefix to some errors: Bad state: (StateError), Invalid argument(s): (ArgumentError), Unsupported operation: (UnsupportedError), Exception: (Exception).
  • For problems that need a longer story, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: dox_core: start of the app
docs.text: Text When What to do APP_KEY is not set. Rundox key:generateand put the key in .env appKey is empty. A warning, or a StateError that stops the app when APP_ENV=production. Run dox key:generate, or set APP_KEY in the env. Unsupported operation: dox_http_native did not load: <reason>. Fix: ... The native HTTP library is missing or from another version (native library ABI <x>, expected <y>). The app stops at start. Do what the Fix: part says. See Troubleshooting. Server started at http://<host>:<port> with <n> isolate (native) Normal start. <host> is the address it listens on: [::] means all interfaces. Nothing. Windows: the native server runs on one isolate Windows has no SO_REUSEPORT. Nothing. Socket.IO runs on <n> isolates: clients should use transports: ['websocket'] ... Socket.IO with more than one isolate and long-polling on. Use a Redis adapter, and transports: ['websocket'] in the client. [dox] isolate <n> error: <error> An error killed a worker isolate. The stack is on the next line. Fix the error. Dox restarts the isolate. [dox] isolate <n> exited, restarting A worker isolate died. A new one starts after 1 second. Look at the error line above it. SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>), port = <port> The port is in use. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: dox_core: routes and controllers
docs.text:
These stop the app at start, so a bad route never reaches a request.

Text When What to do Route <where>: the controller parameter type <T> is not known. Use DoxRequest, a @Dto class, a type from Route.bind, or String, int, double, num, bool for path params. ... A controller parameter has another type, the DTO is not in AppConfig.dtos, or there is no Route.bind<T> for a {param} of the route. Change the type, add the binder, or run dart run build_runner build and set dtos: dtos. Route name "<name>" is used twice: <method> <path> and <method> <path>. Two routes have the same name. Give one of them another name. Invalid argument (name): No route has this name: "<name>" route() or Route.url() with a name that no route has. Check the name and the group name: prefix. Invalid argument(s): Route "<name>" (<path>) needs the param "<param>". route() without a value for a {param}. Pass it in params:. Invalid argument(s): Route "<name>" (<path>) has no param "<key>". ... route() with a param the path does not have. Remove it, or pass it in query:. Bad state: No bound value of type <T> for the route param "<param>". ... req.bound<T>() for a param with no Route.bind, or of another type. Add Route.bind<T>('<param>', ...). Route <where>: the controller has more path params than the route has {...} params (<n>). The method asks for more path params than the path has. Add the {param} to the path, or remove the parameter. Route <where>: a controller can have one @Dto only. Two DTO parameters. Merge them into one DTO. Route <where>: only positional parameters are supported, not named or [optional] ones (<type>). Named or [optional] parameters. Use positional parameters. Use int? with {id?} for an optional param. Route <where>: a controller can not be generic. The handler has type parameters. Remove them. Route <where>: can not read the controller type <type>. Dox can not read the function type of the handler. Use a plain method or function.

docs.title: dox_core: env
docs.text:
Text When What to do EnvException: the env is not valid then - <KEY> is missing AppEnv.load() found a required key with no value. Set the key, or give the getter a default. - <KEY> must be <type>, not "<value>" A value does not fit the getter type. Fix the value. Check for a # comment after it. Env key "<KEY>" is not set and has no default Env.get<int>(), <num>, <double> or <bool> with no value and no default. Set the key, or pass a default. Env key "<KEY>" is not a valid <type>: "<value>" Env.get<int>() (or another type) got text that is not that type. Fix the value.

See Environment variables.

docs.title: dox_core: requests (what the client gets)
docs.text:
An IHttpException with a text message answers {"code":"<errorCode>","message":"<text>"}. The table shows the message text.

Status Message When What to do 404 <METHOD> <path> not found No route matches. Check the method, the path and the router prefix. 404 Not Found A typed path param does not fit, like abc for int id. Send a valid value. 400 The body is not valid JSON A DTO reads a JSON body that does not parse. Send valid JSON. 400 The form body is not valid A urlencoded body that can not be decoded. Fix the client encoding. 415 Unsupported Media Type A DTO reads a body that is not JSON or form data. Send Content-Type: application/json or form data. 413 Payload Too Large The body is bigger than maxBodySize or maxMultipartSize. Send less, or raise the limit. 422 {"_root":"The input has too many items (max 1000) or levels (max 10)"} Form or query keys with more than 1000 list items or 10 levels. Send less nested data. 422 {"<field>":"<message>"} A DTO check failed. See Validation rules. 431 (no text) Native server: request line plus headers over 16 KB. Send smaller headers or cookies. 500 Server Error, code server_error. When APP_ENV is development or local, the body is <error>.toString() as plain text. Any error that is not an IHttpException. It also goes to the report method of the ExceptionHandler. Look at the server log.

docs.title: dox_core: DTOs, storage and config
docs.text: Text When What to do Bad state: <T> is not a known DTO. Add @Dto() to it, rundart run build_runner buildand setdtos: dtos(lib/dtos.g.dart) in AppConfig. req.validate<T>() can not find T. Do what the text says. Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>" A disk in StorageConfig has a driver other than local, s3 or memory. Fix the driver name. Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" needs the "<setting>" setting. It is missing or empty. An s3 disk without bucket, key or secret, on its first use. Set AWS_BUCKET, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Invalid argument(s): invalid file Storage().put() with no extension:, and Dox can not find the type from the bytes. Pass extension: 'pdf'. 403 invalid or expired signature A Route.files() URL without a valid signature, or after expires. Make a new link with Storage().signedUrl(). 404 file not found Storage().stream() or download() of a missing file. Check the path. Invalid argument (trustedProxies): not an ip or cidr: "<value>" A bad entry in AppConfig.trustedProxies. Use an IP, a CIDR like 10.0.0.0/8, or *. Invalid argument (type): must be asc or desc: "<value>" orderBy(column, type) with another direction. Use asc or desc. 400 decrypt_failed AESEncryptor.decode got changed text or a wrong key. It throws DecryptException. req.cookie() catches it and returns null. Check the key. For a cookie, ask the user to log in again.

docs.title: dox_auth
docs.text:
Text When What to do 401 Authentication failed AuthMiddleware finds no token, a bad or expired token, or the user is deleted. Send Authorization: Bearer <token>. Log in again. Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt length ... Hash.verify() with a value that is not a bcrypt hash. See Troubleshooting. Invalid argument(s) (password): Password is too long ... bcrypt with a password over 72 bytes. Limit the length in the DTO.

Auth().attempt() returns null for a wrong password. It does not throw. See Authentication.

docs.title: dox_orm
docs.text: Text When What to do Unsupported operation: dox_postgres_native did not load: <reason>. Dox needs it to talk to Postgres. Fix: ... The native Postgres library did not load. The app stops. Follow the fix in the message. See Postgres native. Unsupported operation: dox_mysql_native did not load: <reason>. Dox needs it to talk to MySQL. Fix: ... The native MySQL library did not load. The app stops. Follow the fix in the message. See MySQL native. PgServerException(<code>): <message> The Postgres server said no, eg. code 23505 for a unique violation. Read code, detail and constraint on the exception. MysqlException(<code>, <sqlState>): <message> An error from MySQL, eg. code 1062 for a duplicate key. Read code and sqlState on the exception. Exception: <name> not found DatabaseConfig.connection (or withConnection()) names a connection that is not in connections. Fix DB_CONNECTION or the map. Exception: Invalid driver or not supported A ConnectionConfig.driver Dox can not open. Use Driver.postgres, Driver.mysql or Driver.sqlite. Invalid argument(s): dox_postgres_native: bad connection config The native driver can not read the connection values. Check host, port, user, database. Invalid argument(s): dox_mysql_native: bad connection config Same, for MySQL. Same. SqliteException with unable to open database file The SQLite folder does not exist. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: dox_orm: schema builder
docs.text: Text When What to do Bad state: foreign key <name>: call on(table) table.foreign('x').references('id') with no .on('table'). Add .on('table'), or use foreignId('x').constrained(). Unsupported operation: postgres: change() of an auto increment column is not supported change() on an id() or increments() column. Write the ALTER by hand with schema.driver.execute(). Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not add a primary key to an existing table primary(...) in schema.table() on SQLite. Make the table again with the key in schema.create(). Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has CHECK constraints A SQLite rebuild (change(), foreign(), dropForeign()) on a table with other CHECKs. Make the new table by hand in the migration. Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has generated columns Same, on a table with generated columns. Same. Bad state: sqlite: table <table> not found A SQLite rebuild of a missing table. Check the table name. Bad state: sqlite: column <table>.<column> not found change() or renameColumn() of a missing column on SQLite. Check the column name. Bad state: sqlite: foreign key <names> not found dropForeign() of a key the table does not have. Check the key name or columns. Bad state: sqlite: rebuild of <table> breaks foreign keys After the rebuild, rows point to missing parent rows. Fix the data first. Unsupported operation: sqlite: change() rebuilds the table, it only runs on a database table.toSql(SqliteGrammar()) with change(). Run it on a database, not as text.

docs.title: dox_migration
docs.text:
Text When What to do Exception: Could not connect to database: <error> The migrator can not open the database. Check DATABASE_URL or the DB_* values. A real env var wins over .env. Unknown migration command: <cmd> (use run, rollback, reset, refresh or status) dart run bin/migrate.dart <cmd> with another command. Use one of the five. Invalid argument(s): Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count> rollback with a bad option. Use --step=2. Bad state: Migration <name> is both a Dart and a .sql migration Two files with the same name in db/migration. Rename or delete one. Bad state: foreign key check failed: <table> points to a missing <parent> row SQLite: a migration left a broken foreign key. Fix the data in the migration. Migrating: <name> / Migrated: <name> Normal progress. Nothing. Migrations are already up to date! Nothing to run. Nothing. Nothing to rollback! No batch to undo. Nothing. No migrations found. status with no migrations. Check db/migration.

See Migration.

docs.title: dox_cache
docs.text:
Text When What to do Invalid argument(s): Cache store "<name>" is not configured Cache().store('<name>') or defaultStore names a missing store. Add the store to CacheConfig.stores, or fix CACHE_STORE. Invalid argument(s): Cache driver "<driver>" of store "<name>" is not supported A store has a driver other than file, memory, redis or null. Fix the driver name. Unsupported operation: <Driver> does not support locks lock() on the file or null store. Use the memory or redis store. Bad state: Cache value of "<key>" is not an integer increment() or decrement() on a value that is not an int. Store an int, or forget() the key. Invalid argument(s): Cache value of "<key>" is bigger than <limit> bytes A Redis value is too big. Store less, or use files or a database. Bad state: RedisDriver.flush needs a prefix. It will not delete the whole database. flush() on a Redis store with an empty prefix. Set a prefix.

See Cache.

docs.title: dox_storage
docs.text:
The text has the form <Exception>: <message> (key: "<key>").

Text When What to do FileNotFoundException: File not found The file is not on the disk. Check the path. Storage() paths start with /, Disk keys do not. PermissionDeniedException: Permission denied The OS (local) or S3 (403) refused it. Check file rights, or the S3 key and bucket policy. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: path traversal is not allowed A key with ... Do not build keys from user input. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: absolute paths are not allowed A Disk key that starts with / or a drive letter. Remove the first /. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: key is empty An empty key. Pass a file name. UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase is not configured Storage().url() on a local disk with no url option. Set url on the disk. UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase and appKey are needed for signed URLs signedUrl() on a local disk with no url, or no APP_KEY. Set both. UnsupportedOperationException: S3 signed URLs must expire within 1 second and 7 days signedUrl() on S3 with a bad expiresIn. Use a time up to 7 days. UnsupportedOperationException: Disk "<name>" is not registered Storage().disk('<name>') with a missing disk. Add the disk to StorageConfig.disks. DriverException: <S3 error> Any other S3 error (network, 500, wrong bucket). Read the S3 code in the text.

See File storage.

docs.title: dox_validation
docs.text:
Text When What to do Bad state: Schema has async rules. Use parseAsync() instead. schema.parse() on a schema with an async rule. Use await schema.parseAsync(). Bad state: Rule "<name>" is async. Use parseAsync() instead. Same, for one AsyncRule. Same. Bad state: This refine is async. Use parseAsync() instead. refine() with an async function and sync parse. Same. Bad state: DTO <name> has an async validate(). Use parseAsync() instead. A DTO with Future<void> validate() checked with a sync call. Use the async call, like req.validate<T>(). docs.title: dox_builder (build_runner)
docs.text:
These stop dart run build_runner build.

Text When What to do The @Dto class <Name> has problems: then a - ... list One or more lines below. Fix each line. - The field <Class.field> must be final. A DTO field is not final. Add final. - The field <Class.field> must be athis.parameter of the unnamed constructor. The field is not set by the constructor. Add this.<field> to the constructor. - A @Dto class needs an unnamed constructor. Only named constructors. Add const Name({...}). - A @Dto class can not extend another class (<Parent>). The DTO extends a class. Copy the fields in. - A @Dto class can not be generic. The DTO has type parameters. Remove them. - The type <T> of <where> is not supported. Use a basic type, an enum, DateTime, RequestFile, a @Dto class, or a List or Map of them. Field type not supported. Change the type. - @<Rule> does not fit the type <T> of <where>. A rule on the wrong type, like @Email() on an int. Move the rule, or change the type. - @Length on <where> needs min:, max: or both. @Length() with no limit. Add min: or max:. - The @Regex on <where> is not a valid regex: <reason> The pattern does not compile. Fix the pattern. - @MaxSize on <where> needs a size like '2MB' (units B, KB, MB, GB), not "<text>". Bad size text. Use '2MB'. - The Maybe field <where> needs the defaultconst Maybe.missing(). A Maybe<T> field without that default. Add it. - <where> can not have both @Lowercase and @Uppercase. Both on one field. Keep one. - The validate method of <Name> must take one DtoErrors:void validate(DtoErrors errors). Wrong validate signature. Use that signature. Two @Dto classes are named <Name>: in <a> and <b>. Dox finds DTOs by name, so rename one. Two DTOs with the same class name. Rename one. Env getter "<name>" has type <T>. Use String, int, double, num, bool, Uri, Duration, an enum or List<String>. A @DoxEnv getter with another type. Change the type. @DoxModel can only be used on a class. / @DoxEnv can only be used on a class. The annotation is on something else. Put it on a class. Conflicting outputs were detected ... build_runner cache is out of date. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Native libraries (build hooks)
docs.text:
Printed during dart pub get, dox serve or dox build. <pkg> is dox_http_native, dox_postgres_native or dox_mysql_native.

There is no fallback. When a library is missing, the app stops with the reason and the fix. dox_http_native stops at start. The database drivers stop when the ORM opens the database.

Text When What to do <pkg>: no native library for <os>-<arch>. No ready build for this OS and CPU. Install Rust. <pkg>: download <file>: <status> / <pkg>: download <file> failed: <error> The GitHub download failed. Check the network, then dart pub get again. <pkg>: sha256 of <file> does not match The downloaded file is not the expected one. Delete .dart_tool and try again. <pkg>: cargo build failed The build from source failed. Read the cargo output below it. Bad state: <pkg>: <path> does not exist The lib_path user define points to a missing file. Fix the path in pubspec.yaml. Unsupported operation: dox_http_native can not detach the socket. Use NativeWebSocket.upgrade for a WebSocket. Code called detachSocket() on a response. Rust owns the socket. For a WebSocket use NativeWebSocket.upgrade(request).

See Native server.

docs.title: dox_socketio
docs.text:
Printed to stderr. The connection or the request fails, the app keeps running.

The client gets 500. Check the client version and transport. dox_socketio: redis publish failed: <error> The Redis adapter could not publish. docs.title: HTTP exceptions
docs.text:
An exception that extends IHttpException turns into an HTTP error answer.

You can throw it or return it from a middleware or a controller.

IHttpException is in packages/dox-annotation/lib/src/core_annotation.dart:

abstract class IHttpException {
  int code = 500;
  String errorCode = 'server_error';
  dynamic message = 'Server Error';

  dynamic toResponse() {
    if (message is Map) {
      return message;
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'code': errorCode, 'message': message.toString()};
  }
}

docs.title: The classes
docs.text:
Every class takes the named parameters message, errorCode and code. The table shows the defaults.

Class Package Status code errorCode Default message Dox throws it when BadRequestException dox_core 400 bad_request Bad Request the body can not be read, like JSON that is not valid UnAuthorizedException dox_auth 401 unauthorized Authentication failed AuthMiddleware finds no valid token NotFoundHttpException dox_core 404 not_found Not Found a typed path param does not fit ({id} is not an int) PayloadTooLargeException dox_core 413 payload_too_large Payload Too Large the body is bigger than maxBodySize or maxMultipartSize UnsupportedMediaTypeException dox_core 415 unsupported_media_type Unsupported Media Type a DTO reads a body that is not JSON and not form data ValidationException dox_core 422 validation_failed {} (a Map) a DTO or req.validate() finds bad input InternalErrorException dox_core 500 server_error Server Error never by itself; for your own use QueryException dox_core 500 sql_query_error Error in sql query never by itself; for your own use

Source files: packages/dox-core/lib/exception/*.dart and packages/dox-auth/lib/src/auth_exception.dart.

docs.title: What the client gets
docs.text:
responseDataHandler in packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_response_handler.dart sends the answer:

  1. The status is set to code.
  2. The body is toResponse().
  3. The body is sent as JSON with Content-Type: application/json.

A text message gives a JSON body with the errorCode and the message:

throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json

{"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}

A Map message is sent as it is, with no code key. ValidationException always has a map, one entry per field:

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json

{"email":"The email is not a valid email","name":"The name is required"}

A request for a path that has no route answers like a NotFoundHttpException with the message <METHOD> <path> not found: {"code":"not_found","message":"GET /nothing not found"}. Your responseHandler gets it too, so you can change its shape.

To send your own JSON shape from one exception, pass a map:

throw NotFoundHttpException(
  message: <String, dynamic>{'error': 'not_found', 'message': 'Blog not found'},
);

Other errors: any Exception or Error that is not an IHttpException gets 500 with {"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}. When APP_ENV is development or local, the body is error.toString() as text instead. It is also passed to the report method of the exception handler. An IHttpException is not reported.

A ValidationException from dox_validation (thrown by schema.parse() in a controller) is turned into the 422 ValidationException of dox_core with the same errors.

docs.title: Make your own
docs.text:
Extend IHttpException and set the three fields in the constructor:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ForbiddenException extends IHttpException {
  ForbiddenException({
    dynamic message = 'Forbidden',
    String errorCode = 'forbidden',
    int code = HttpStatus.forbidden,
  }) {
    super.code = code;
    super.errorCode = errorCode;
    super.message = message;
  }
}

Override toResponse() to give every error of your app the same JSON shape.

More examples are on the Response page.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
Check each item before you deploy.

Items marked Dox limit are things Dox does not do for you. You must handle them outside Dox.

docs.title: Secrets and config
docs.text: Check How Read more APP_KEY is set, 32 characters and secret dox key:generate, or a random value of exactly 32 characters in the real env. It signs JWT tokens and encrypts cookies. Never use the value from .env.example. Encryption APP_ENV=production An empty APP_KEY, a key that is not exactly 32 characters, or an old sample key stops the app at start (StateError). Only APP_ENV development, local or test logs a warning instead. Env reference The env is complete Run dox env:check in CI or before the deploy. It exits with code 1 when a key is missing or bad. CLI No secrets in the image or in git .env in .dockerignore and .gitignore. Pass values as env vars (docker run -e, env_file:, systemd EnvironmentFile=). dox build copies .env.example only. Docker No comments after values in .env The app strips # note, but migrations keep it in the value. Put comments on their own line. Env reference

docs.title: Auth and passwords
docs.text: Check How Read more JWT tokens expire JwtAuthDriver.expiresIn is 1 hour by default. Pick a time that fits your app, like JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey), expiresIn: Duration(hours: 12)). Authentication You can not revoke one token Dox limit. There is no token list on the server. To log out everyone, change APP_KEY. Authentication Passwords are hashed user.password = Hash.make(input) (bcrypt). Never store or encrypt a plain password. Hashing The hash is never sent List<String> get hidden => <String>['password']; in the user model. The JWT payload is user.toJson(), and anyone can read it. Authentication Passwords have a max length bcrypt throws on input over 72 bytes. Add @MaxLength(72) to the password field of the DTO. It counts characters, so non-ASCII text can still pass 72 bytes. Troubleshooting

docs.title: HTTP and network
docs.text: Check How Read more HTTPS at the proxy Dox has no TLS server. Run Caddy or nginx in front. Keep the app port private. Deployment trustedProxies is set behind a proxy AppConfig(trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1']), or the proxy network, like '172.16.0.0/12'. Without it, req.ip() is the proxy and req.scheme() is http. Do not use ['*'] when the app port is public. App config Body limits are on Keep maxBodySize (10 MB) and maxMultipartSize (100 MB), or lower them. Set the same limit in the proxy: client_max_body_size 100m; Request CORS has real origins CORSConfig(origin: 'https://my.app'), or a list like <String>['https://my.app', 'https://admin.my.app']. With a list, Dox sends back only the request origin when it is in the list. CORS No credentials: true with origin: '*' The new project's cors.dart has origin: '*' and credentials: true with enabled: false. When you turn CORS on, set a real origin first. CORS Rate limiting Add RateLimit(...) to login and other busy routes. Use a Redis cache store, so all servers share the counts. Or limit at the proxy, see below. Rate limiting Security headers Add const SecurityHeaders() to globalMiddleware. Security headers gzip at the proxy Keep compress: false. Turn on gzip in Caddy (encode gzip) or nginx (gzip on;). Performance OpenAPI docs Off in production by default (on only for APP_ENV development or local). Do not set enabled: true for a private API. OpenAPI

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text: Check How Read more AOT binary, not dart run dox build, then run build/bundle/bin/server. Keep bin/ and lib/ together. Not dart compile exe. Deployment Native server loads The app starts and the start line says (native). When the library does not load, the app stops with dox_http_native did not load and the fix. Native server Native database driver loads The app starts and the database works. When the library does not load, the app stops with dox_postgres_native did not load (or mysql) and the fix. Postgres native Isolates = cores Keep the default totalIsolate (Platform.numberOfProcessors), or set APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE to the cores the container really gets. Use fewer when the database runs on the same machine. Isolate Shared state across isolates Cache: redis, not memory. Socket.IO: a Redis adapter and transports: ['websocket']. Isolate A supervisor restarts the process Docker restart: unless-stopped, or systemd Restart=always. Dox restarts a dead worker isolate, but not the main isolate. Deployment Writable temp folder Uploads over 1 MB go to a temp file. A FROM scratch image needs /tmp with mode 1777. Docker Uploads live on a volume or S3 The local disk writes to storage/. Mount it as a volume, or use the s3 disk. File storage

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Check How Read more Postgres or MySQL for a busy app SQLite has one connection per isolate, and a query blocks the isolate. Use it for small apps only. With SQLite use an absolute file path, never :memory: with many isolates. Database Migrations run once per deploy The new project runs Migrator(migrations: migrations).migrate() in bin/server.dart before startServer(). Or run dart run bin/migrate.dart run (or dox migrate) in CI. Do one, not both at the same time on many machines. Migration Migrations use the right database dox_migration reads .env and the real env. A real env var wins, but a key that is only in an old .env is still used. Do not ship a .env next to the binary, or give Migrator(config: ...) your own config. Migration Small MySQL migrations MySQL saves CREATE, ALTER and DROP at once. A failed migration can leave half the changes. One table change per migration. Migration Pool size fits the database extra: {'maxConnectionCount': 10}. The Postgres and MySQL drivers share one pool per process, so the total is the pool size, not isolates x pool size. Keep it under the database max_connections. Database Query logging is off debug: true prints every query. The new project's database.dart sets debug only when APP_ENV=development. Database Backups Dox limit. Dox has no backup tool. Use pg_dump, mysqldump, managed database snapshots, or a copy of the SQLite file (with the -wal file, or sqlite3 app.db ".backup x.db"). Test a restore.

docs.title: Logs and errors
docs.text: Check How Read more JSON logs LoggerConfig(enabled: true, prettyPrint: false). The new project sets prettyPrint only when APP_ENV=development. App config Log level Set LOG_LEVEL=warn to print only warnings and errors. App config Access logs in one place LogMiddleware writes one line per request, every 20 ms. A hard kill can lose the last lines. Turn it off when the proxy already logs requests. Performance Errors go to your tracker Extend ExceptionHandler and set AppConfig.exceptionHandler. Any non-HTTP error is passed to its report method. The client gets 500 with server_error. The error text is sent only when APP_ENV is development or local. Error handling

docs.title: Health and shutdown
docs.text: Check How Read more Health route Add Route.health('/health', checks: ...) with a database check, so the load balancer knows when the app can not serve. Health check Graceful shutdown On SIGTERM or SIGINT, Dox stops taking connections and lets open requests finish, in every isolate. Set shutdownTimeout below the kill timeout of your platform. The ORMService closes the database in its DoxShutdown hook, and Dox closes the cache stores. Close your own connections in a DoxShutdown service. Deployment Zero downtime deploys Run two processes (or machines) behind the proxy. Restart one at a time. Deployment

docs.title: Rate limit at the proxy
docs.text:
You can also limit at the proxy. Then bad clients never reach the app.

nginx:

# in http { }
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s;

# in server { location / { } }
limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
limit_req_status 429;

Caddy needs the caddy-ratelimit plugin (build Caddy with xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit):

example.com {
  rate_limit {
    zone api {
      key    {remote_host}
      events 100
      window 1m
    }
  }
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

Note

The proxy must see the real client IP. When there is a load balancer in front of the proxy, set the real IP module of the proxy first.

docs.title: Request and response
docs.text:
A compact list of the members of DoxRequest and DoxResponse.

Examples and explanations are on the Request and Response pages.

docs.title: DoxRequest
docs.text: Source: packages/dox-core/lib/http/request/dox_request.dart. It implements IDoxRequest from dox_annotation. A middleware gets an IDoxRequest. A controller gets a DoxRequest. The members marked IDoxRequest are on both.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest validate<T>({Source? source}) Future<T> The request checked with the DTO T. Throws the 422 ValidationException on bad input. Throws StateError when T is not in AppConfig.dtos. no validateSchema<O>(Schema<O> schema) Future<O> Query and body checked with a fluent dox_validation schema. no all() Map<String, dynamic> Query and body together. Body wins on the same key. yes only(List<String> keys) Map<String, dynamic> Only these keys from all(). A missing key gives null. yes input(String key) dynamic One value from all(). yes has(String key) bool true when the key is there and its text is not empty. yes add(String key, dynamic value) void Adds a value to all() and body. yes merge(Map<String, dynamic> values) void Adds many values to all() and body. yes body Map<String, dynamic> The parsed body (JSON or form fields). Files are RequestFile. no query Map<String, dynamic> The query string. no param Map<String, dynamic> The route params, like {'id': '5'}. no pathParams Map<String, String> The route params as text. null values are left out. no requestBody RequestBody The body as it was read, for DTOs. no isJson() bool The content type is JSON. yes isFormData() bool The content type is form data (multipart/form-data or urlencoded). yes toJson() Map<String, dynamic> all() with files replaced by their file name. Lets jsonEncode(req) work. yes

docs.title: Headers, cookies and client
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest header(String key) String? One header. null when it is not there. yes headers Map<String, dynamic> Every header. Many values of one name are joined. yes httpHeaders HttpHeaders The dart:io headers object. no contentType ContentType? The parsed Content-Type. yes cookie(String key, {bool decrypt = true}) String? One cookie. Decrypted with appKey unless decrypt: false. yes ip() String The client IP, or unknown. From X-Forwarded-For only behind a trusted proxy. yes scheme() String http or https. From X-Forwarded-Proto only behind a trusted proxy. no isSecure() bool scheme() is https. no clientIp String? The client IP, or null. no userAgent() String The User-Agent header, or unknown. yes host() String The Host header, or unknown. yes origin() String? The Origin header. yes referer() String? The Referer header. yes locale String? The first language of Accept-Language, like th. null when there is none or it is *. no auth IAuth? The auth object set by AuthMiddleware, or null. yes

docs.title: Route and raw request
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest method String The HTTP method in upper case. yes uri Uri The request URI. yes route RouteData The matched route. no getRouteData() RouteData Same as route. yes getRouteIdentifier() String base64 of <method>|<domain><path>. Useful as a cache or rate limit key. yes httpRequest HttpRequest The dart:io request. Use it for raw access. yes

docs.title: DoxResponse
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-core/lib/http/response/dox_response.dart. Every setter returns the same DoxResponse, so calls chain.

Member Returns What it does DoxResponse(dynamic content) DoxResponse The constructor. content can be a String, number, Map, List, a JSON serializable object, a Stream<List<int>>, a File, a StreamFile or a DownloadableFile. response([dynamic content]) DoxResponse Top level helper. Same as DoxResponse(content). statusCode(int code) DoxResponse Sets the status. Default 200. content(dynamic content) DoxResponse Replaces the content. getContent() dynamic The content as it was given. stream(Stream<List<int>> stream) DoxResponse Sets a byte stream as content. contentType(ContentType type) DoxResponse Sets Content-Type. A File without it gets the type from its extension. header(String key, dynamic value) DoxResponse Adds one header. withHeaders(Map<String, dynamic> values) DoxResponse Replaces every header set so far with this map. cookie(DoxCookie cookie, {bool setExpire = false}) DoxResponse Adds a Set-Cookie header. setExpire: true sends the cookie as expired, which removes it. cache(Duration duration) DoxResponse Sets Cache-Control: max-age=<seconds>. process(HttpRequest request) dynamic Internal. Writes headers, status, cookies and the body.

How the content is sent (responseDataHandler in packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_response_handler.dart):

Content Sent as null an empty body String text, as it is Map, List, number, bool, object with toJson() JSON, Content-Type: application/json DateTime its ISO 8601 text File streamed, with Content-Length, Accept-Ranges and one Range supported StreamFile streamed with its content type DownloadableFile streamed with Content-Disposition: attachment Stream<List<int>> streamed chunk by chunk IHttpException its status and toResponse(), see HTTP exceptions other Exception or Error 500 with toString() as text

A plain value returned from a controller (not a DoxResponse) is sent the same way. It only goes through a DoxResponse when AppConfig.responseHandler is set, or when it is a File, StreamFile or DownloadableFile.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Real problems, with the text you see, the cause and the fix.

The texts come from the source code.

docs.title: The native HTTP library did not load
docs.text:
Symptom. The app stops at start with this error:

Unsupported operation: dox_http_native did not load: <reason>.
Fix: install Rust (cargo, see https://rustup.rs), then run the app again ...

At build time (dart pub get, dox serve or dox build) you may also see one of these:

dox_http_native: no native library for <os>-<arch>. Install Rust (cargo) to build it from source.
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext>: 404
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> failed: <error>
dox_http_native: sha256 of dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> does not match
dox_http_native: cargo build failed

Cause. The build hook of dox_http_native (hook/build.dart in its repo) tries, in this order: the lib_path user define, a local native/target/release build, the GitHub release download, and cargo build. None worked. Common reasons:

  • No internet during dart pub get, or the release has no build for your OS and CPU (there are builds for macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 and arm64, Windows x64).
  • Rust is not installed, so the fallback cargo build can not run.
  • You compiled with dart compile exe. It does not run build hooks, so no native library is in the binary.
  • The <reason> is native library ABI <x>, expected <y>: the library on disk is from another version of the package.

Fix. Pick one:

  1. Install Rust with rustup and run dart pub get again. The hook builds the library with cargo.
  2. When the reason is an ABI mismatch and you set lib_path, rebuild that library: cargo build --release in the native folder of the dox-http-native repo.

  3. Download the library from the GitHub release v<version> of dartondox/dox-http-native yourself and point to it in the root pubspec.yaml:

    hooks:
  user_defines:
    dox_http_native:
      lib_path: /path/to/libdox_http_native.so

  4. Build with dox build (it runs dart build cli), not with dart compile exe.

The native database drivers find their library the same way. When it does not load, the app stops too, with:

dox_postgres_native did not load: <reason>.
dox_mysql_native did not load: <reason>.

The fix is the same as above, with the dox-postgres-native or dox-mysql-native repo.

See Native server, Postgres native and MySQL native.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text:
Symptom. At start:

SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>), port = 3000

<code> is -1000 minus the OS error: -1048 on macOS, -1098 on Linux.

Cause. Another process listens on the port. Often it is an old bin/server.dart that dox serve did not stop, or a second copy of the app.

Fix. Find and stop the process, or use another port.

lsof -i :3000          # macOS and Linux: who has the port
kill <pid>

Or set APP_PORT=3001 in .env (a new project reads it into serverPort).

docs.title: build_runner: conflicting outputs
docs.text:
Symptom. dox build_runner:build, dox serve or dox build stops with a build_runner message that starts with Conflicting outputs were detected, and names files like lib/dtos.g.dart or lib/app/models/user/user.model.g.dart.

Cause. The generated .g.dart files are on disk, but .dart_tool/build does not know them. This happens after a git clone with committed .g.dart files, after deleting .dart_tool, or after a Dart SDK update.

Fix. Delete the build cache and build again:

rm -rf .dart_tool/build
dart run build_runner build

If that is not enough, delete the named .g.dart files and build again. New build_runner versions have no --delete-conflicting-outputs flag, so the Dox CLI does not pass it.

docs.title: Ambiguous import: Uuid, Name or Schema
docs.text:
Symptom. The analyzer or the build says a name like Uuid, Name, Range, Image or Schema is an "ambiguous import".

Cause. dox_core exports the validation rule names (Uuid, Name, Range, Image, ...). Another import has a class with the same name, like package:uuid. dox_orm also has a Schema class.

Fix. Hide the name you do not use in that file:

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' hide Uuid;
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

docs.title: A .env value with #
docs.text:
A # after a space starts a comment. The comment is not part of the value.

APP_PORT=3000 # dev port   -> 3000
DB_PASSWORD=abc#123        -> abc#123 (no space before the #)
DB_PASSWORD="abc # 123"    -> abc # 123 (quotes keep the #)

When a value must have # in it (a space, then #), put the value in quotes. The quotes are removed.

docs.title: Hash.verify throws on a bad hash
docs.text:
Symptom.

Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt length (The length should be greater than or equal to 28): "..."

or

Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt version: "..."

or, when the password is long:

Invalid argument(s) (password): Password is too long (The length should be less than or equal to 72): "..."

Cause. Hash.verify(password, hash) calls BCrypt.checkpw from the bcrypt package. It throws an ArgumentError when hash is not a bcrypt hash (it must start with $2 and be at least 28 characters), for example when the column holds a plain password, an empty string or a hash from another algorithm. It also throws when the password is longer than 72 bytes.

Fix.

  • Make sure every stored password went through Hash.make(). A plain password in the column is a bug in the code that saved it.

  • Check the hash before you compare it, and treat a bad one as a failed login:

    bool ok = hash.startsWith(r'$2') && Hash.verify(password, hash);

  • Refuse passwords longer than 72 bytes in your DTO, for example @Length(max: 72).

For normal login use Auth().attempt() from dox_auth. See Hashing.

docs.title: MySQL 8 login fails
docs.text:
Symptom. The connection to MySQL 8 is refused at login, while the same user works from the mysql client. Often the user was made with the default caching_sha2_password plugin.

Cause. caching_sha2_password needs either TLS or the server RSA public key to send the password. A client that has neither can not log in.

Fix. The Dox MySQL driver (dox_mysql_native) supports caching_sha2_password (MySQL 8.4) and MariaDB 11. Check these settings on the connection in lib/config/database.dart:

Setting What to do Remote host without TLS Turn on useSSL: true. useSSL: true The server must have TLS on. host, port, user, password A wrong value gives the same login error. DB_PORT is 3306 by default for MySQL.

As a last resort, change the user on the server:

ALTER USER 'app'@'%' IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password BY 'secret';

docs.title: SQLite: the database file
docs.text:
Symptom. An SqliteException with unable to open database file, or an empty database after dox build.

Cause. database is a file path. A relative path is relative to the folder you start the app from. dox build tells you to run cd build/bundle && ./bin/server, so dox.sqlite is then build/bundle/dox.sqlite. SQLite makes a missing file, but not a missing folder.

Fix.

  • Use an absolute path, or make the folder first.
  • Set it with DB_NAME (a new project reads it): DB_NAME=/var/lib/my_app/dox.sqlite.
  • Migrations use DB_DATABASE or DB_NAME as the path too. Use the same value for both.

:memory: and isolates

:memory: opens a new empty database in each isolate. With totalIsolate above 1, every isolate sees different data. Use a file, or totalIsolate: 1.

Dox opens a file database with journal_mode = WAL, synchronous = NORMAL, foreign_keys = ON and busy_timeout = 5000 (change it with extra: {'busyTimeout': ...}).

docs.title: dox: command not found after dart pub global activate
docs.text:
Symptom.

zsh: command not found: dox

right after dart pub global activate dox ^3.0.0-alpha.

Cause. dart pub global activate puts the dox script in $HOME/.pub-cache/bin. That folder is not in your PATH.

Fix. Add it to your shell profile and open a new terminal:

export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"

On Windows the folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Pub\Cache\bin.

docs.title: Other startup errors
docs.text: Short errors, like a bad route, a missing DTO or a bad env key, are in the Error index.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
This page shows how to log users in with dox_auth and protect routes with a JWT token.

dox_auth checks an email and a password against your user table. It gives back a JWT token. The client sends this token in the Authorization header. AuthMiddleware reads the token and loads the user from the database.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_auth

A new app made with the dox CLI already has it.

docs.title: 1. Hide the password in the model
docs.text:
The token holds the user data as JSON, and anyone can read a JWT. So the password hash must never be in toJson(). Put it in hidden:

lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users')
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}

docs.title: 2. Set up the auth service
3. Add the routes
docs.text:
AuthMiddleware protects a route. When the token is missing or not valid, the request stops with 401 Authentication failed.

lib/routes/api.dart
Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/register', (AuthController c) => c.register);
Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/login', (AuthController c) => c.login);
Route.get<AuthController>('/auth/user', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (AuthController c) => c.user]);

docs.title: 4. Write the controller
5. Send the token from the client
docs.text:
GET /auth/user
Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: Read the user
docs.text:
After AuthMiddleware, req.auth holds the login.

Code What it gives req.auth an IAuth?. null when the route has no AuthMiddleware req.auth?.isLoggedIn() true when a user is loaded req.auth?.user<User>() the user model req.auth?.toJson() the user as a map, without hidden fields

docs.title: The Auth class
docs.text:
Method What it does Auth.initialize(AuthConfig) sets the config. Call it once, in a service Auth(guard: 'admin') uses another guard from guards. Without guard, it uses defaultGuard await Auth().attempt(credentials) finds the user and checks the password. Gives a token, or null Auth().login(user) gives a token for this user, with no password check user<T>() the user after attempt or login isLoggedIn() true when there is a user

attempt searches only by the fields in identifierFields. It runs bcrypt also when no user is found, or when the user has no password, so the answer time does not tell whether an email has an account. It returns null when the password is not a String, when no identifier is given, or when the password does not match.

docs.title: AuthProvider
docs.text: Option Default What it does model required a function that makes a new model, like () => User() identifierFields ['email'] the fields attempt searches by passwordField 'password' the column with the bcrypt hash

docs.title: JwtAuthDriver
docs.text: Option Default What it does secret required the key that signs tokens, like SecretKey(env.appKey). An empty key throws ArgumentError. A key shorter than 32 bytes also throws in production, and prints a warning in development, local and test. Make one with dox key:generate or openssl rand -hex 32 algorithm JWTAlgorithm.HS256 the signing algorithm expiresIn Duration(hours: 1) how long a token is valid issuer null the iss claim. When set, verifyToken also checks it hashRounds 10 the bcrypt cost of your stored hashes. Use the same value as Hash.rounds userCacheTtl null (off) keep the user of a token in memory for this time. See below

docs.title: More than one guard
docs.text:
Each guard has its own driver and its own user model. For example, users and admins in two tables:

AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'web',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'web': AuthGuard(
      driver: JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey)),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
    'admin': AuthGuard(
      driver: JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey)),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => Admin()),
    ),
  },
);

Pick the guard by name:

String? token = await Auth(guard: 'admin').attempt(credentials);

Route.get<AdminController>('/admin', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(guard: 'admin'), (AdminController c) => c.index]);

The token keeps the guard name in its aud claim. So a token from the web guard does not work on the admin guard, even with the same secret. An unknown guard name throws an ArgumentError.

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• The token is not secret. Anyone with the token can read user.toJson(). Keep private columns in hidden.
  • You can not cancel one token. A token works until it expires. If you change the secret (your APP_KEY), all tokens stop working.
  • The user is loaded on each request, by the id in the token. A deleted user can not log in, even with a valid token.
  • userCacheTtl skips that query. With Duration(seconds: 30), a deleted or changed user is seen only after 30 seconds. Each isolate has its own cache. Requests in that time share one user object, so do not change it per request.
  • Login does not block the server. attempt runs bcrypt in another isolate.
  • Hash passwords before you save them. See Hashing.

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
This page shows how to let a web page on another domain call your API.

A browser blocks a request from https://my.app to https://api.my.app by default. The API must send CORS headers to allow it. Dox adds these headers from CORSConfig.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
The config is in lib/config/cors.dart. Pass it to AppConfig(cors: cors).

lib/config/cors.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  enabled: true,
  origin: 'https://my.app',
  methods: <String>['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],
  headers: <String>['Content-Type', 'Authorization'],
  exposeHeaders: <String>['Content-Disposition'],
  credentials: true,
  maxAge: 600,
);
lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  cors: cors,
  // ...
);

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Each option sets one response header. An option that is null sends no header.

Option Header Value enabled - true adds the headers to every route. Default: true origin Access-Control-Allow-Origin one origin, a List<String> of origins, or '*' for all methods Access-Control-Allow-Methods a List<String> or a text like 'GET,POST'. '*' allows all headers Access-Control-Allow-Headers a List<String> or a text. '*' allows all exposeHeaders Access-Control-Expose-Headers the response headers the page may read credentials Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true lets the browser send cookies maxAge Access-Control-Max-Age how many seconds the browser keeps the preflight answer

For methods, headers and exposeHeaders, a list is joined with commas.

docs.title: More than one origin
docs.text:
Access-Control-Allow-Origin accepts only one origin or *. So when origin is a list, Dox checks the Origin header of the request:

  • The origin is in the list: Dox sends back that one origin.
  • The origin is not in the list: Dox sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. The browser blocks the call.
  • The list has '*': Dox sends *.

With a list, Dox also sends Vary: Origin. This tells caches that the answer depends on the origin.

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  origin: <String>['https://my.app', 'https://admin.my.app'],
);

credentials with *

Browsers do not send cookies when origin is '*'. When you need cookies, set origin to your real front-end URL.

docs.title: Preflight requests
docs.text: Before some requests, the browser sends an OPTIONS request. You do not need an OPTIONS route for this. Dox answers it with 204 No Content and the CORS headers. It uses the CORS setting of the route that the browser asks about.

docs.title: Turn CORS on or off for some routes
docs.text:
enabled is the default for all routes. Change it for a group of routes:

lib/routes/api.dart
// CORS headers only on these routes (use with enabled: false)
Route.enabledCors(() {
  Route.get<PostController>('/public/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
});

// no CORS headers on these routes
Route.disabledCors(() {
  Route.post<WebhookController>('/webhooks/stripe', (WebhookController c) => c.handle);
});

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
This page shows how to encrypt and decrypt text with AESEncryptor.

Dox uses AESEncryptor to encrypt cookies with your APP_KEY. You can also call it yourself.

docs.title: Encrypt and decrypt
docs.text:
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

String secret = env.appKey; // 32 characters

String encoded = AESEncryptor.encode('Hello world', secret);
String decoded = AESEncryptor.decode(encoded, secret); // 'Hello world'
  • encode returns base64 text.
  • The same text gives a different output each time.
  • decode throws DecryptException when the text was changed, or the key is wrong. It is a 400 Bad Request error.
  • The secret must be 16, 24 or 32 bytes long (AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256). Another length makes encode throw.

Make a new 32-character APP_KEY with the CLI:

dox key:generate

docs.title: Cookies
docs.text:
DoxCookie encrypts its value with APP_KEY by default. req.cookie(key) decrypts it.

return response().cookie(DoxCookie('theme', 'dark'));  // encrypted
DoxCookie('theme', 'dark', encrypt: false);             // plain text

String? theme = req.cookie('theme');                    // decrypted
String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false);      // as sent

req.cookie(key) returns null when the cookie was changed, was made with another APP_KEY, or was made for another cookie name. The cookie name is bound to the encrypted value, so a value can not be copied from one cookie to another.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
AESEncryptor uses AES-GCM.

  • Each message gets a new random 12-byte nonce.
  • The output is base64 of nonce + encrypted text + tag.
  • The 16-byte tag checks the message. If someone changes one byte, decode throws.

To store passwords, do not encrypt them. Hash them. See Hashing.

docs.title: Hashing
docs.text:
This page shows how to hash passwords with Hash and check them later.

A hash is one-way. You can not turn it back into the password. Hash uses bcrypt with a new random salt each time. It is in package:dox_core/dox_core.dart.

docs.title: Hash a password
docs.text:
Hash the password before you save it.

user.password = Hash.make(body.password);
await user.save();

The result looks like $2a$10$.... It holds the salt, so you only store this one string. The same password gives a different hash each time.

docs.title: Check a password
docs.text:
bool ok = Hash.verify('secret', user.password!);

Hash.verify(password, hashedPassword) returns true when the password matches. It returns false when the password does not match, or when hashedPassword is not a valid bcrypt hash (for example an empty string).

docs.title: Without blocking the server
docs.text:
Hash.make and Hash.verify block the request isolate while bcrypt runs. In a request handler, use the async versions. They run bcrypt in another isolate.

user.password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
bool ok = await Hash.verifyAsync('secret', user.password!);

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
Hash.rounds is the bcrypt cost for new hashes. The default is 10. Each step up doubles the time.

Hash.rounds = 12;
String hash = Hash.make('secret', rounds: 12); // or per call

Old hashes keep their own cost, so they still verify. If you change it, also set hashRounds on JwtAuthDriver to the same value. See Authentication.

docs.title: With login
docs.text: You do not need Hash.verify for normal login. Auth().attempt() from dox_auth finds the user and checks the password with bcrypt. See Authentication.

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• Never store or encrypt a plain password. Hash it.
  • Never send the hash to the client. Put the column in the model hidden list.
  • bcrypt is slow on purpose, so guessing is slow too. Do not hash in a loop on hot paths.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text: RateLimit is a middleware that stops a client that sends too many requests. Use it on login, sign up and other routes that bots like to hammer.

docs.title: Limit a route
Limit every route
docs.text:
Put it in globalMiddleware:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    RateLimit(max: 120),
  ],
  // ...
);

docs.title: Count by API key, not by ip
docs.text:
key picks who is counted. The default is req.ip().

RateLimit(
  max: 100,
  key: (DoxRequest req) => req.header('X-Api-Key') ?? req.ip(),
)

The key is any String, so you can also count by user id after your auth middleware.

Behind a proxy

Behind Caddy, nginx or a load balancer, every request comes from the proxy ip. Then all clients share one count. Add the proxy to AppConfig.trustedProxies, so req.ip() is the real client ip. See App config.

docs.title: Two limits on the same key
docs.text:
Two RateLimit with the same max and per share one counter. Give one a name to keep them apart:

Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/login', <dynamic>[
  RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'login'),
  (AuthController c) => c.login,
]);
Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/register', <dynamic>[
  RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'register'),
  (AuthController c) => c.register,
]);

docs.title: Where the counts live
docs.text:
The counts are kept in the cache:

  • When the default cache store is Redis, the counts are in Redis. All isolates and all servers share them. Use this in production.
  • Else the counts are in memory. Each isolate has its own counts. With 4 isolates a client can send up to 4 x max requests.

To use one store by name, pass store:

RateLimit(max: 10, store: 'redis')

docs.title: How it counts
docs.text: It is a fixed window. With per: Duration(minutes: 1) the count starts at 0 at the start of each minute. So a client can send max requests at the end of one minute and max more at the start of the next. That is fine for most apps. For a hard limit, use a smaller window.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Middleware
  • Security headers
  • Production checklist
