docs.title: Security headers
docs.text: SecurityHeaders is a middleware that adds safe HTTP headers to every answer. The browser reads them and blocks some common attacks, like showing your page in a frame on another site.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
Put it in globalMiddleware:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const SecurityHeaders(),
  ],
  // ...
);

Every answer now has these headers:

Header Default value What it does X-Content-Type-Options nosniff The browser does not guess the file type. X-Frame-Options DENY No site can show your page in a frame. Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin Other sites only see your domain, not the full url. Permissions-Policy camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() The page can not use the camera, the microphone or the location. Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin A page of another site that opens yours can not reach it. Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains The browser uses only https for one year. Sent only on https requests.

Content-Security-Policy is off by default. A good policy depends on your pages.

docs.title: Change or turn off a header
docs.text:
Each header has an option. Give a new value to change it, or null to turn it off:

const SecurityHeaders(
  frameOptions: 'SAMEORIGIN', // allow frames from your own site
  permissionsPolicy: null, // do not send this header
  contentSecurityPolicy: "frame-ancestors 'none'",
  extra: <String, String>{'Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy': 'same-origin'},
)
Option Header contentTypeOptions X-Content-Type-Options frameOptions X-Frame-Options referrerPolicy Referrer-Policy permissionsPolicy Permissions-Policy crossOriginOpenerPolicy Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy strictTransportSecurity Strict-Transport-Security contentSecurityPolicy Content-Security-Policy extra any other headers, name to value

docs.title: HSTS behind a proxy
docs.text:
Dox serves plain http. The https part is done by a proxy (Caddy, nginx, a load balancer). Dox sends Strict-Transport-Security only when the request came in over https. It knows that from the X-Forwarded-Proto: https header, and it only believes this header from a trusted proxy. So add your proxy to AppConfig.trustedProxies:

AppConfig(trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1']);

Without it, Dox never sends HSTS. See App config.

Note

Middleware runs only for routes that exist. A 404 for an unknown url does not get these headers.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Middleware
  • CORS
  • Rate limiting

docs.title: Controller
docs.text: A controller holds the code that answers a route. It can be a class method, a static method or a plain function.

docs.title: Class based controller
docs.text:
Make one with the CLI:

dox make:controller Blog

It writes lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart.

lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class BlogController {
  String index(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'all blogs';
  }
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get<BlogController>('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.index);

@Inject() puts the controller in the container. Run dart run build_runner build after you add one. The constructor can ask for services and repositories. See Dependency injection.

docs.title: Static method
docs.text:
class AppController {
  static String ping(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

Route.get('/ping', AppController.ping);

docs.title: Function based controller
docs.text:
String listBlog(DoxRequest req) {
  return 'all blogs';
}

Route.get('/blogs', listBlog);

docs.title: Resource controller
docs.text:
A resource controller has the 7 methods that Route.resource uses.

Make one with the CLI:

dox make:controller Blog -r
lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class BlogController {
  /// GET /resource
  Future<dynamic> index(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/create
  Future<dynamic> create(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// POST /resource
  Future<dynamic> store(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> show(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}/edit
  Future<dynamic> edit(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// PUT|PATCH /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> update(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// DELETE /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> destroy(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.resource('blogs', BlogController);

You can delete methods you do not need. Route.resource skips them. See Routing: resource routes.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
A controller asks for what it needs by type. Dox fills each parameter.

Route.put<UserController>('/teams/{teamId}/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.update);

class UserController {
  Future<User> update(int teamId, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
}
Parameter type Dox gives DoxRequest the request a @Dto class the checked body or query. See Validation. String, int, double, num, bool the path params, in the order of the route the same types with ? an optional path param ({id?}). null when it is not in the URL. a @DoxModel class the model, loaded by the route param. See route model binding. an @Inject() class the instance from the container

Rules:

  • The order of parameters is free. Path params are matched by position: the first path-param parameter gets the first {...} in the route.
  • DoxRequest is not needed. Add it only when you use it.
  • At most one @Dto parameter.
  • Only positional parameters. Named and [optional] parameters are not supported.
  • A catch-all {path*} param is a String.
  • The same rules work for static methods and plain functions.
  • Dox reads the parameter types once, at start. It does not use dart:mirrors.

Path param types. Dox converts the text from the URL:

  • int: "42" is 42. "abc" or "4.5" answers 404 Not Found.
  • double, num: "4.5" is 4.5.
  • bool: true or 1 is true. false or 0 is false.
  • Any other text answers 404 too.
  • Path params are checked first. When one is wrong, the DTO is not checked.

Checked at start. The server does not start when:

  • a parameter type is not in the list above (did you run dart run build_runner build?),
  • the method has more path-param parameters than the route has {...} params.

docs.title: What to return
docs.text: Return a String, a Map, a model, a File and more. See Response.

docs.title: Dependency injection
docs.text: Dox has a container. It makes your classes and gives each constructor what it needs. You do not register classes by hand. Put @Inject() above a class, and dox_builder adds it to the container. Dox does not use dart:mirrors. All the wiring is generated code.

docs.title: A full example
docs.text:
A repository reads the database. A service holds the business logic. A controller answers the route.

lib/app/repositories/user.repository.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class UserRepository {
  Future<User?> find(int id) => User().find(id);
}
lib/app/services/user.service.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/repositories/user.repository.dart';

@Inject()
class UserService {
  UserService(this.users);

  final UserRepository users;

  Future<User> show(int id) async {
    User? user = await users.find(id);
    if (user == null) throw NotFoundHttpException();
    return user;
  }
}
lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/services/user.service.dart';

@Inject()
class UserController {
  UserController(this.service);

  final UserService service;

  Future<User> show(int id) => service.show(id);
}
lib/routes/api.dart
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get<UserController>('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.show);
  }
}

Run the builder:

dart run build_runner build

It writes lib/container.g.dart. Give it to the app once:

lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:my_app/container.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  container: registerContainer,
  // ...
);

That is all. GET /api/users/5 makes the repository, the service and the controller, and calls show(5).

docs.title: The generated file
docs.text:
lib/container.g.dart has one function. Each class gets a factory that calls its constructor.

lib/container.g.dart
// GENERATED CODE - DO NOT MODIFY BY HAND
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart' as i1;
import 'package:my_app/app/repositories/user.repository.dart' as i2;
import 'package:my_app/app/services/user.service.dart' as i3;
import 'package:my_app/routes/api.dart' as i4;
import 'package:my_app/services/orm_service.dart' as i5;
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart' as i6;

void registerContainer(IocContainer c) {
  c.singleton<i1.UserController>(
    (IocContainer c) => i1.UserController(c.get<i3.UserService>()),
  );
  c.singleton<i2.UserRepository>((IocContainer c) => i2.UserRepository());
  c.singleton<i3.UserService>(
    (IocContainer c) => i3.UserService(c.get<i2.UserRepository>()),
  );
  c.router<i4.ApiRouter>((IocContainer c) => i4.ApiRouter());
  c.service<i5.ORMService>((IocContainer c) => i5.ORMService());
  c.bindModel<i6.User>((String id) {
    int? key = int.tryParse(id);
    if (key == null) return null;
    return i6.User().find(key);
  });
}

Do not edit it. Run the builder again after you add a class.

docs.title: Lifetime
docs.text:
• @Inject(): one instance per isolate. It is made on first use.
  • @Inject(singleton: false): a new instance each time it is asked for.

Dox runs one server per isolate. Isolates do not share objects. So each isolate runs registerContainer and has its own instances. Do not keep state in a singleton that all isolates must see. Use the cache or the database for that.

docs.title: Constructor parameters
docs.text:
Each constructor parameter is found by its type.

  • Positional and named parameters both work.
  • An optional parameter whose type is not in the container keeps its default value.
  • A nullable parameter whose type is not in the container gets null.
  • Any other parameter whose type is not in the container stops the build.

docs.title: Routes to controller methods
docs.text:
Give the controller type, then a function that picks the method:

Route.get<PostController>('/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
Route.post<PostController>('/posts', (PostController c) => c.store);
Route.put<PostController>('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.update);
Route.delete<PostController>('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.destroy);

The controller comes from the container. Dox gets it once per isolate, at start. A request does no extra work. .name(), groups and middleware lists work the same:

Route.get<PostController>('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.show).name('posts.show');
Route.get<AuthController>('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (AuthController c) => c.me]);

You can leave out <PostController>. Dox then finds the controller by the parameter type: Route.get('/posts', (PostController c) => c.index).

For resource routes, pass the class:

Route.resource('posts', PostController);

The method still gets its parameters as usual: DoxRequest, a @Dto, path params and bound models. See Controller: parameters.

docs.title: Handler parameters
docs.text:
A controller method (or a plain route function) can ask for any class of the container:

Route.get('/stats', (StatsService stats) => stats.today());

A singleton is read once, at start. A singleton: false class is made on each request.

docs.title: Route model binding
docs.text:
Every @DoxModel class gets a binder in lib/container.g.dart. When a handler has a parameter of a model type, Dox loads the model by its primary key.

Route.get<PostController>('/posts/{post}', (PostController c) => c.show);

@Inject()
class PostController {
  Post show(Post post) => post;
}
  • The route param with the name of the model is used: {post} for Post, {blogPost} for BlogPost.
  • When there is no such param, the next route param in order is used, like {id}.
  • A missing row answers 404.
  • An int key that is not a number answers 404, with no database call.
  • A route without a parameter of the model type does not load the model.
  • A binder from Route.bind wins over this one. See Routing: route model binding.

docs.title: Routers and services
docs.text:
You do not need @Inject() on them.

  • Every class that extends Router is found. Its routes are registered at start.
  • Every class that implements DoxService is found. Its setup() runs at start, in every isolate.

Their constructors get parameters from the container too.

They run in the order of their file path, then the order in the file. To pick the order, list them in AppConfig:

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  container: registerContainer,
  services: <DoxService>[ORMService()], // runs first
  routers: <Router>[ApiRouter()],       // registered first
);

A listed class comes first. The others follow. No class runs twice. A listed service is also the instance that the container gives.

docs.title: Use the container in code
docs.text:
Dox().ioc is the container of the current isolate.

UserService users = Dox().ioc.get<UserService>();
Method What it does get<T>() the instance of T. Throws when T is not registered. has<T>() true when T is registered singleton<T>(factory) one instance per isolate, made on first use factory<T>(factory) a new instance on each get instance<T>(value) value is the instance, eg. a config object override<T>(value) replace T, eg. with a fake in a test clearOverrides() remove every override

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Replace a class with a fake before the app starts:

setUpAll(() async {
  Dox().ioc.override<UserRepository>(FakeUserRepository());
  client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
});

tearDownAll(() async {
  await client.close();
  Dox().ioc.clearOverrides();
});

An override stays when the app registers its classes again. Call it before DoxTestClient.start. Controllers get their objects once, at start.

docs.title: Build errors
docs.text:
The build stops with a clear message when:

  • a required parameter has a type that is not in the container,
  • classes need each other in a circle. The message shows the chain, like A -> B -> C -> A,
  • @Inject() is on an abstract class or a generic class,
  • a class has no unnamed constructor.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Dox finds classes in lib/ only.
  • The container is keyed by the class. It does not map an interface to a class.
  • Two classes with the same name in two files both work. But use the typed route style (Route.get<C>(...)) for them. They can not be handler parameters, because Dox can not tell them apart by name.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Every error that a route throws goes to one place: the exception handler. It does two things:

  • report(error, stackTrace) logs the error.
  • render(error, req) decides what the client gets.

docs.title: The default answer
docs.text:
You do not need to set anything. With the default handler:

Error Status Body an IHttpException, like NotFoundHttpException its code {"code": "not_found", "message": "Not Found"} a ValidationException (bad input) 422 the field errors, like {"name": "The name is required"} a URL with no route 404 {"code": "not_found", "message": "GET /x not found"} any other error 500 {"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}

For a 500, the error text is sent only when APP_ENV is development or local. In production the client never sees it, because it can hold SQL, file paths or hosts.

report is called for every error that is not an IHttpException. An IHttpException is a normal answer (like 404), so it is not logged. The default report prints the error and the stack with the logger.

See HTTP exceptions for the built-in exception classes.

docs.title: Your own handler
docs.text:
Extend ExceptionHandler. Override one method or both.

lib/app/exception_handler.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class AppExceptionHandler extends ExceptionHandler {
  const AppExceptionHandler();

  @override
  void report(Object error, StackTrace stackTrace) {
    // send it to your error tracker
    print('ERROR $error\n$stackTrace');
  }

  @override
  dynamic render(Object error, HttpRequest req) {
    if (error is PaymentRequiredException) {
      return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Please pay'})
          .statusCode(402);
    }
    // everything else: the default answer
    return super.render(error, req);
  }
}

Set it in AppConfig:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  exceptionHandler: const AppExceptionHandler(),
  // ...
);

docs.title: What render can return
docs.text:
render returns anything a controller can return: a DoxResponse, a map, a string. Return the error itself (this is what super.render does) to get the default answer.

req is the raw HttpRequest. It is there even when the error came before Dox read the body. Use it to read headers, like req.headers.value('accept').

If render itself throws, Dox logs that error and sends the default answer. The client always gets a response.

docs.title: Errors outside a request
docs.text: Some errors do not belong to a request. For example a future that nobody awaits, or an error in a service shutdown(). Dox passes them to report too. The server keeps running.

docs.title: The response handler
docs.text:
The responseHandler of AppConfig still runs after render. It sees every response, also error responses. Use render to change errors, and responseHandler to change all responses (for example, to add a header).

See Custom errors for a full example with your own exception classes.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text: Middleware is code that runs before the controller. Use it for checks like login, logging or rate limits.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
A middleware gets the request. It then does one of these:

  • Return the request. Dox goes on to the next middleware, then to the controller.
  • Return something else (a String, a Map, a response(...)). Dox sends it as the response. The controller does not run.
  • Throw an exception, like NotFoundHttpException(). Dox sends the error response. See Response: errors.

A middleware can be async. Dox waits for it.

docs.title: Class based middleware
docs.text:
Create one with the CLI. It writes lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart.

dox make:middleware Logger
lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class LoggerMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path}');
    return req; // go on to the next middleware
  }
}

Then put it on a route:

lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get<WebController>('/ping', <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware(), (WebController c) => c.pong]);

Note

handle takes an IDoxRequest, not a DoxRequest.

docs.title: Function based middleware
docs.text:
A function that takes a DoxRequest also works as middleware.

lib/app/http/middleware/api_key.middleware.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

dynamic apiKeyMiddleware(DoxRequest req) {
  if (req.header('X-Api-Key') != 'secret') {
    return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Unauthorized'}).statusCode(401);
  }
  return req;
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get<WebController>('/ping', <dynamic>[apiKeyMiddleware, (WebController c) => c.pong]);

docs.title: Many middleware on one route
docs.text:
Put them in the list before the controller. They run from left to right. You can mix class and function middleware.

Route.get<WebController>('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  apiKeyMiddleware,
  (WebController c) => c.pong, // the controller is always last
]);

docs.title: Middleware for a group of routes
docs.text:
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()], () {
  Route.get('/me', controller.me);
  Route.post('/logout', controller.logout);
});

docs.title: Middleware for a router or for all routes
docs.text:
For one router, set its middleware list:

lib/routes/api.dart
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()];

  @override
  void register() {
    // every route here runs LoggerMiddleware
  }
}

For all routes, set globalMiddleware in the app config:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
  // ...
);

The order is: global middleware, then router middleware, then group middleware, then route middleware.

flowchart LR
    Q["Request"] --> G["Global<br>globalMiddleware"]
    G --> R["Router<br>middleware getter"]
    R --> P["Group<br>Route.middleware"]
    P --> T["Route<br>list before the controller"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
    C --> S["Response"]
    G & R & P & T -.->|"returns a value or throws"| S

Built-in middleware

  • LogMiddleware from dox_core writes one JSON log line per request. Body fields and headers whose name has password, secret, token, authorization, cookie or api_key in it (upper or lower case) are logged as [REDACTED]. Change the list with redact:. The new project turns it off when APP_ENV is production.
  • AuthMiddleware from dox_auth checks the JWT token. See Authentication.
  • RateLimit from dox_core answers 429 when a client sends too many requests. See Rate limiting.
  • SecurityHeaders from dox_core adds safe headers like X-Frame-Options to every answer. See Security headers.

docs.title: Request
docs.text: This page shows how to read input, files, headers and cookies from a request.

docs.title: Typed input (recommended)
docs.text:
Ask for a DTO in your controller. Dox reads the body (or the query for GET), checks it, and gives you a typed object.

Route.put('/users/{id}', controller.update);

class UserController {
  Future<User?> update( // (1)!
    int id, // (2)!
    UpdateUser input, // (3)!
  ) async {
    User? user = await User().find(id);
    user?.name = input.name;
    await user?.save();
    return user;
  }
}
  1. The return value is the response. Dox waits for a Future. A String is sent as text. A Map or a model is sent as JSON.
  2. A path param. It is {id} from the route. /users/abc answers 404, because abc is not an int.
  3. A DTO. Dox reads the body, checks it, and builds the object before this method runs.

Bad input gets 422 before your method runs. See Validation.

docs.title: Raw input
docs.text:
Add a DoxRequest parameter to read the raw values. These values are not checked.

class ApiController {
  String sayHello(DoxRequest req) {
    String? name = req.input('name');
    return 'Hello $name';
  }
}
Code Gives req.input('name') one value from the query string or the body. The body wins when both have the key. req.all() all values from the query string and the body, as a Map req.only(<String>['name', 'email']) only these keys req.has('name') true when the key is there and not empty req.body the body only (JSON, form data) req.query the query string only req.add('key', value), req.merge({...}) add values, for example in a middleware

docs.title: Route params
docs.text: Ask for a path param as a typed parameter, like int id in the example above. The raw text values are also in req.param, like req.param['id']. See Controller: parameters.

docs.title: Form data (File)
docs.text:
An uploaded file is a RequestFile. The request must be multipart/form-data. Put the file in a DTO, so Dox checks its type and size:

@Dto()
class UploadImage {
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('5MB')
  final RequestFile image;

  const UploadImage({required this.image});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}

class ApiController {
  Future<Map<String, String>> uploadImage(UploadImage input) async {
    String uploadedPath = await input.image.store('images');
    return <String, String>{'filename': uploadedPath};
  }
}

Without a DTO, req.input('image') gives the RequestFile. It is not checked.

docs.title: RequestFile
docs.text:
RequestFile file = req.input('video');

file.filename;        // name from the client
file.filetype;        // content type, like video/mp4
file.extension;       // mp4
file.length;          // size in bytes
await file.size;      // size in KB
file.stream();        // read it in chunks
await file.store('videos');              // save to storage. returns the path
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4'); // move it. returns the new File
await file.bytes;     // the whole file in memory. avoid for big files

Save the file before you return

A file up to 1 MB stays in memory. A bigger file is written to a temp file while it arrives. The temp file is deleted when the response is sent. So call store, moveTo or stream before your controller returns.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
A body that is too big gets 413 Payload Too Large. Dox checks Content-Length first. It also counts the bytes while it reads the body.

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,        // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,  // form-data uploads, default 100 MB
);

Set the same limit in your proxy, like client_max_body_size in nginx.

docs.title: Headers
docs.text:
String? token = req.header('X-Token');
Map<String, dynamic> all = req.headers;

req.userAgent();  // User-Agent header
req.host();       // Host header
req.origin();     // Origin header, or null
req.referer();    // Referer header, or null
req.isJson();     // true for a JSON body
req.isFormData(); // true for multipart/form-data
req.locale;       // first language of Accept-Language, like 'th', or null

docs.title: Cookies
docs.text:
String? token = req.cookie('token');                 // decrypted value
String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false);   // value as sent

See Response to set a cookie.

docs.title: Client IP and scheme
docs.text:
req.ip();       // client IP
req.scheme();   // http or https
req.isSecure(); // true for https

Behind a proxy, req.ip() shows the proxy, not the client. Set trustedProxies in AppConfig to fix it. See Deployment.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: This page shows what a controller can return, and how to set the status, headers and cookies.

docs.title: Return a value
docs.text:
Return the value from your controller. Dox turns it into the response.

You return The client gets a String the text a Map or a List JSON a model, a list of models, a serializer JSON (from toJson()) a DateTime the ISO 8601 text an IHttpException, like NotFoundHttpException() its status code and its message (text, or JSON for a Map) a File (from dart:io) the file, streamed a Stream<List<int>> the bytes, streamed StreamFile, DownloadableFile from Storage() the file, streamed response(...) full control: status, headers, cookies 
// JSON
Map<String, String> hello(DoxRequest req) {
  return <String, String>{'message': 'hello world!'};
}

// a model
Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
  return Blog().find(id);
}

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Throw or return an exception to answer with an error.

Exception Status BadRequestException() 400 NotFoundHttpException() 404 PayloadTooLargeException() 413 UnsupportedMediaTypeException() 415 ValidationException() 422 InternalErrorException() 500

Each one takes message:, errorCode: and code::

throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');

The client gets 404 with {"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}. code is the errorCode. A Map message is sent as it is.

For another status, extend IHttpException:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ForbiddenException extends IHttpException {
  ForbiddenException({String message = 'Forbidden'}) {
    super.code = HttpStatus.forbidden;
    super.errorCode = 'forbidden';
    super.message = message;
  }
}

Any other error gets 500. It is also passed to the exception handler.

docs.title: Files and big responses
docs.text:
Return a File or a Stream<List<int>>. Dox sends it in chunks. It does not load it all into memory.

  • A File sets Content-Type (from the file name), Content-Length and Accept-Ranges.
  • It answers Range: bytes=... with 206 Partial Content. Video players can seek, and downloads can resume.
  • Storage().stream() and Storage().download() on the local disk also stream the file.
import 'dart:io';

// a file from disk
Route.get('/video', (DoxRequest req) => File('storage/video.mp4'));

// a download from Storage
Future<DownloadableFile> download(DoxRequest req) async {
  // sends Content-Disposition, so the browser saves the file
  return Storage().download('report.pdf');
}

// a stream from Storage
Future<StreamFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Storage().stream('photo.jpg');
}

See File Storage.

docs.title: The response() helper
docs.text:
Use response(content) when you need to set the status, headers or cookies. All methods return the response, so you can chain them.

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

DoxResponse store(DoxRequest req) {
  return response(<String, String>{'status': 'created'})
      .statusCode(201)
      .header('X-Request-Id', 'abc')
      .contentType(ContentType.json);
}
Method Does statusCode(201) sets the status code. Default 200. header('X-Key', 'value') adds one header withHeaders({...}) replaces all headers set before contentType(ContentType.html) sets Content-Type (ContentType is from dart:io) cache(Duration(minutes: 5)) sets Cache-Control: max-age=300 cookie(DoxCookie(...)) sets a cookie content(value) changes the body stream(byteStream) sends a Stream<List<int>> as the body

docs.title: Cookie
docs.text:
// set a cookie
DoxCookie cookie = DoxCookie('theme', 'dark');
return response('ok').cookie(cookie);

// set a cookie with options
DoxCookie token = DoxCookie(
  'token',
  'value',
  maxAge: Duration(days: 7), // sent as Max-Age in seconds. default 1 hour
  httpOnly: true, // default true: page scripts can not read it
  secure: true,   // default: Secure only when the request came over https
  path: '/',
);
return response('ok').cookie(token);

// delete a cookie
return response('ok').cookie(DoxCookie('token', ''), setExpire: true);

To read a cookie, see Request: cookies.

Encrypt and decrypt

By default, Dox encrypts the cookie value with APP_KEY, and decrypts it when you read it. To turn this off, use DoxCookie(key, value, encrypt: false) to set it, and req.cookie(key, decrypt: false) to read it.

docs.title: Change every response
docs.text:
To change every response in one place (for example, to add a header), set a responseHandler in AppConfig.

lib/app/http/handler.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ResponseHandler extends ResponseHandlerInterface {
  @override
  DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res) {
    return res.header('X-Powered-By', 'Dox');
  }
}
lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),
  // ...
);

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
A route connects a URL and an HTTP method to the code that answers it.

This is the path of one request through the router:

flowchart LR
    Q["Request<br>GET /blogs/42"] --> B["Router<br>method, host, path"]
    B -->|no match| N["404"]
    B -->|match| P["Params as text<br>req.param"]
    P --> M["Middleware"]
    M -->|returns a value| S["Response"]
    M -->|returns the request| T["Typed params, DTO<br>int id"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
    C --> S

docs.title: Where routes live
docs.text:
Routes are in the lib/routes folder. Each file has one Router class. The prefix of the router is added in front of all its routes.

lib/routes/api.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong'); // GET /api/ping
  }
}

Dox finds every Router class by itself. It is in lib/container.g.dart after dart run build_runner build. To pick the order of routers, list them in routers: of AppConfig. See Dependency injection: routers and services.

The leading / in a path is optional. 'ping' and '/ping' are the same route.

docs.title: Route methods
docs.text:
Route.get<BlogController>('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.index);
Route.post<BlogController>('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.store);
Route.put<BlogController>('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.update);
Route.patch<BlogController>('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.update);
Route.delete<BlogController>('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.destroy);

Info

There are also Route.options, Route.copy, Route.view, Route.link, Route.unlink, Route.purge, Route.lock, Route.unlock and Route.propfind.

A HEAD request runs the GET route of the same path. The answer has the status and headers of GET, with no body.

docs.title: The handler
docs.text:
The second argument is the code that answers the request. It can be:

// a function
Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');

// a controller method. The controller comes from the container.
Route.get<WebController>('/ping', (WebController c) => c.pong);

@Inject()
class WebController {
  String pong(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

// a list: middleware first, the controller last
Route.get<WebController>('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  (WebController c) => c.pong,
]);

In a list, the last item is the controller. The items before it are middleware. (WebController c) => c.pong picks the method. Dox calls it once per isolate, at start. See Dependency injection.

See Controller for the parameters a handler can ask for.

docs.title: Route params
docs.text:
Put a param in {}. Ask for it as a typed parameter in the controller.

Route.get('/blogs/{id}', controller.show);

class BlogController {
  Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }
}

/blogs/abc answers 404, because abc is not an int. See Controller: parameters for all the rules.

docs.title: Optional param
docs.text:
{name?} can be missing. Use a nullable type.

Route.get('/posts/{page?}', (int? page) {
  return 'page ${page ?? 1}'; // GET /posts and GET /posts/2 both match
});

docs.title: Catch-all param
docs.text:
{name*} matches the rest of the path, with slashes.

Route.get('/docs/{page*}', (String page) {
  return page; // GET /docs/a/b/c gives 'a/b/c'
});

docs.title: Group routes
docs.text:
// by prefix
Route.group('/blogs', () { // (1)!
  Route.get('/', controller.index);     // GET /blogs
  Route.get('/{id}', controller.show); // (2)!
});

// by domain
Route.domain('dartondox.com', () { // (3)!
  Route.get('/ping', controller.ping);
});

// by middleware
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () { // (4)!
  Route.get('/me', controller.me);
  Route.post('/logout', controller.logout);
});
  1. /blogs goes in front of every path in the callback. Dox puts one / between the parts. 'blogs' and '/blogs/' work the same.
  2. Makes GET /blogs/{id}.
  3. These routes match only when the Host header is dartondox.com. Other hosts get 404.
  4. AuthMiddleware runs before me and logout. It runs after the global and router middleware.

Groups can be nested. Route.group('blogs', ...) with Route.get('all', ...) makes /blogs/all.

A group can also add a prefix to the route names inside it, with name:.

To turn CORS on or off for some routes, see CORS.

docs.title: Resource routes
docs.text:
One line makes the usual CRUD routes for a controller.

Route.resource('blogs', BlogController);

BlogController is a class from the container. A controller object works too: Route.resource('blogs', BlogController()).

Method Path Controller method Route name GET /blogs index blogs.index GET /blogs/create create blogs.create POST /blogs store blogs.store GET /blogs/{id} show blogs.show GET /blogs/{id}/edit edit blogs.edit PUT, PATCH /blogs/{id} update blogs.update DELETE /blogs/{id} destroy blogs.destroy

The name comes from the path: / becomes ., and {params} are left out. So Route.resource('users/{user}/posts', ...) gives users.posts.index. Pass name: to pick another one: Route.resource('blogs', BlogController, name: 'posts').

A method that the controller does not have is skipped. No route is made for it. Any other error from the controller is not hidden. It stops the app at start, so you see it. See Resource controller to make one with the CLI.

docs.title: Named routes
docs.text:
Give a route a name with .name(). Then build its URL from the name, so a path lives in one place.

Route.get('/users/{id}', controller.show).name('users.show');

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5});
// /users/5

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5}, query: <String, Object>{'tab': 'posts'});
// /users/5?tab=posts

route() gives the path. Route.url() does the same. Param values are URL encoded. A missing {name?} param is left out.

A group can put a prefix in front of the names inside it:

Route.group('admin', () {
  Route.get('users', controller.index).name('users'); // admin.users
}, name: 'admin.');

Dox stops with a clear error when:

  • two routes have the same name (at start),
  • route() gets a name that no route has,
  • a {param} of the path has no value, or params has a key the path does not have.

docs.title: Route model binding
docs.text:
A binder turns a route param into a value before the controller runs, for example a model from the database. Add it with Route.bind, before the routes that use it.

Route.bind<User>('user', (String id) => User().find(id));

Route.get('/users/{user}', (DoxRequest req, User user) {
  return user;
});

Every route with a {user} param now runs the binder first. The binder gets the raw text from the URL. It returns the value, or null when there is none. null answers 404, the same way as a thrown NotFoundHttpException.

There are two ways to read the value:

  • Ask for a parameter of the bound type, like User user. Dox matches it by type, so it can be at any place in the parameter list.
  • Read it from the request: req.bound<User>('user'). This also works in a controller that only takes DoxRequest.

Other path params still work next to it:

Route.get('/users/{user}/posts/{page}', (User user, int page) {
  return user.posts(page);
});

The binder runs after the middleware, so an auth middleware can stop the request before any database call.

A @DoxModel class does not need Route.bind. Dox makes a binder for it in lib/container.g.dart. See Dependency injection: route model binding. Route.bind wins when both exist.

docs.title: Serve storage files
docs.text:
Route.files(path) serves the files of a storage disk at GET <path>/{key*}. By default only signed URLs work. Other requests get 403. See File Storage.

Route.files('files');
Route.files('public', disk: 'local', signed: false);

An html, svg, xml or javascript file is sent as a download (Content-Disposition: attachment) with Content-Security-Policy: sandbox. So a script in an uploaded file does not run on your site. Every file response also has X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, so the browser does not guess another type.

For user uploads, download: true sends every file as a download, also images and PDFs:

Route.files('uploads', download: true);

docs.title: Request body for the docs
docs.text:
post, put and patch take a body: schema. It shows in the OpenAPI docs. It does not check the request. To check input, use a DTO.

Route.post('/posts', controller.store, body: v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'title': v.string().min(3),
}));

docs.title: Serializer
docs.text:
A serializer sets the JSON shape of a response: which keys the client gets, their names and their values. It works with any Dart type: a model, a plain class, or a map.

Tip

You do not always need a serializer. A controller can return a model, a Map or a List as it is. See Response. To only hide some model fields, use hidden.

docs.title: Create a serializer
docs.text:
dox make:serializer Blog

This makes lib/app/http/serializers/blog.serializer.dart. The file is for a model with the same name. Change the type to use it for something else.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Extend Serializer<T> and write convert. convert gets one value of type T and gives back one JSON object.

lib/app/http/serializers/blog.serializer.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

import '../../../app/models/blog/blog.model.dart';

class BlogSerializer extends Serializer<Blog> {
  BlogSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Blog m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'uid': m.id,
      'title_en': m.title,
    };
  }
}

Return the serializer from a controller. Dox sends its toJson().

lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart
class BlogController {
  Future<BlogSerializer> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    List<Blog> blogs = await Blog().all();
    return BlogSerializer(blogs); // a list
  }

  Future<BlogSerializer> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    Blog? blog = await Blog().find(id);
    return BlogSerializer(blog); // one model
  }
}

The response of show:

{
  "uid": 1,
  "title_en": "This is title"
}

What you give, and what the client gets:

You give The client gets one value of type T one JSON object a List<T> a JSON list ([] when the list is empty) null (for example, find found nothing) null any other type null

The list type must be List<T>

A List<dynamic> is not a List<T>, so the response is null. This happens with a list from jsonDecode. Call .cast<T>() first. See JSON from another API.

docs.title: Change values
docs.text:
convert is plain Dart. You can format dates, join fields and add new keys.

lib/app/http/serializers/user.serializer.dart
class UserSerializer extends Serializer<User> {
  UserSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(User m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'id': m.id,
      'name': '${m.firstName} ${m.lastName}',
      'is_active': m.status == 'active',
      'joined_at': m.createdAt?.toIso8601String(),
    };
  }
}

docs.title: A serializer inside a serializer
docs.text:
Use one serializer for a relation inside another. Load the relation first, for example with preload.

lib/app/http/serializers/comment.serializer.dart
class CommentSerializer extends Serializer<Comment> {
  CommentSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Comment m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'id': m.id,
      'content': m.content,
      'user': UserSerializer(m.user).toJson(), // null when there is no user
    };
  }
}

Future<CommentSerializer> index(DoxRequest req) async {
  List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('user').all();
  return CommentSerializer(comments);
}

docs.title: With pagination
docs.text:
page.data is a List<User>. Put the serializer output in place of data.

Future<Map<String, dynamic>> index(ListUsers query) async {
  Pagination<User> page = await User()
      .orderBy('id', 'desc')
      .paginate(currentPage: query.page, perPage: query.perPage);
  return <String, dynamic>{
    ...page.toJson(),
    'data': UserSerializer(page.data).toJson(),
  };
}

See Pagination for the full example.

docs.title: Examples without models
docs.text: T can be any type. You do not need the ORM.

docs.title: A plain Dart class
Rows from the query builder
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.table(...) gives rows as maps, not models. Use Serializer<Map<String, dynamic>> to pick and rename the keys.

lib/app/http/serializers/sales_report.serializer.dart
class SalesReportSerializer extends Serializer<Map<String, dynamic>> {
  SalesReportSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Map<String, dynamic> row) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'product': row['name'],
      'sold': row['total'],
    };
  }
}

Future<SalesReportSerializer> report(DoxRequest req) async {
  List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('orders')
      .selectRaw('name, count(*) as total')
      .groupBy('name')
      .get();
  return SalesReportSerializer(rows);
}

docs.title: JSON from another API
docs.text:
jsonDecode gives a List<dynamic>. Cast it to the type of the serializer first.

Future<SalesReportSerializer> remote(DoxRequest req) async {
  String body = await fetchReport(); // your HTTP call
  List<dynamic> rows = jsonDecode(body);
  return SalesReportSerializer(rows.cast<Map<String, dynamic>>());
}

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • CLI: dox make:serializer

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
This page lists every annotation you can put on a @Dto field. See Validation for how DTOs work.

How to read the tables:

  • Code is the error code. Use it in @Dto(messages: ...) and in a MessageResolver.
  • Message is the default English text. {field} is the last key of the path.
  • Every annotation also takes message:. It wins over every other message.
  • All limits include the limit itself, unless the table says "exclusive".
  • On a List<T> field, a value rule checks each item. Only the list rules check the list itself.

docs.title: Type errors
docs.text:
These have no annotation. They come from the field type.

Code When Message required a required field is missing, null, or "" The {field} is required string not a string The {field} must be a string integer not a whole number The {field} must be an integer numeric not a number (double, num) The {field} must be a number boolean not a bool The {field} must be a boolean date not an ISO 8601 date The {field} must be a date in not a name of the enum The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} array not a list The {field} must be an array object not an object (nested DTO, Map) The {field} must be an object file not a file The {field} must be a file unrecognized_keys unknown key, with @Dto(strict: true) The {field} field is not allowed

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
For String fields (and List<String> items).

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @Length(min: 3, max: 50) length_between The {field} must be between {min} and {max} characters minLength, maxLength @Length(min: 6, max: 6) length The {field} must be exactly {length} characters minLength, maxLength @MinLength(3) min_length The {field} must be at least {min} characters minLength @MaxLength(50) max_length The {field} may not be greater than {max} characters maxLength @Email() email The {field} is not a valid email format: email @Url() url The {field} must be a url format: uri @Uuid() uuid The {field} is invalid uuid format: uuid @Ip() ip The {field} must be an ip address anyOf ipv4 / ipv6 @Regex(r'[a-z]+') regex The {field} format is invalid pattern @In(['a', 'b']) in The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} enum @NotIn(['root']) not_in The {field} field cannot be {value} not: {enum} @StartsWith('dox') start_with The {field} must start with {prefix} pattern @EndsWith('.dev') end_with The {field} must end with {suffix} pattern @Alpha() alpha The {field} must be an alphabetic pattern @AlphaNumeric() alpha_numeric The {field} must be only alphabetic and number pattern @AlphaDash() alpha_dash The {field} must be only alphabetic and dash pattern

Details:

  • @Length has min: and max:. Both are optional, but you must give one. With only min: it acts like @MinLength, with only max: like @MaxLength.
  • Length counts characters (Unicode code points). é counts as 1.
  • @Url() needs http or https and a host.
  • @Uuid() takes any version. Upper or lower case.
  • @Regex(pattern, {message}) must match the whole value. You do not need ^ and $. The regex is checked when the generator runs. A bad regex stops the build.
  • @Alpha(), @AlphaNumeric() and @AlphaDash() use ASCII letters a-z, A-Z. @AlphaDash() also allows - and _.
  • @In and @NotIn compare exactly (case matters).

docs.title: Change text
docs.text:
These change the value before the rules run. They always run in this order, wherever you put them: @Trim, then @Lowercase or @Uppercase, then the "empty string is missing" check.

Annotation Does @Trim() removes spaces at the start and the end @Lowercase() makes the text lower case @Uppercase() makes the text upper case @AllowEmpty() keeps "" as a value. Without it, "" counts as missing.

They have no error and no JSON Schema output. @Lowercase() and @Uppercase() together stop the build.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
For int, double and num fields (and list items).

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @Min(18) min The {field} must be greater than or equal {min} minimum @Max(100) max The {field} must be less than or equal {max} maximum @Range(1, 10) between The {field} must be between {min} and {max} minimum, maximum @Positive() greater_than The {field} must be greater than 0 exclusiveMinimum: 0 @GreaterThan(0.5) greater_than The {field} must be greater than {min} (exclusive) exclusiveMinimum @LessThan(100) less_than The {field} must be less than {max} (exclusive) exclusiveMaximum @In([1, 2, 3]) in The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} enum @NotIn([0]) not_in The {field} field cannot be {value} not: {enum}

The values are num. @Min(1.5) on an int field stops the build.

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
For List<T> fields. These check the list, not the items.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @MinItems(1) min_items The {field} must have at least {min} items minItems @MaxItems(5) max_items The {field} may not have more than {max} items maxItems @UniqueItems() unique_items The {field} must not have duplicate items uniqueItems: true

@UniqueItems() works for String, numbers, bool, enums and DateTime. On a list of DTOs it stops the build.

docs.title: Dates
docs.text:
For DateTime fields.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @After('2000-01-01') after The {field} must be a date after {date} format: date-time @Before('now') before The {field} must be a date before {date} format: date-time
  • The value is an ISO 8601 date, or 'now' (the time of the request).
  • Both are exclusive: @After('2000-01-01') does not accept 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z.
  • To compare two fields (end after start), use validate().

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
For RequestFile and List<RequestFile> fields.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @MaxSize('2MB') max_size The {field} may not be larger than {max} maxLength (bytes) @Mimes(['pdf', 'png']) mimes The {field} must be a file of type: {types} contentMediaType @Image() image The {field} must be an image contentMediaType: image/*
  • @MaxSize units: B, KB, MB, GB. 1KB = 1024 bytes. A bad size text stops the build.
  • @Mimes takes file extensions. Dox finds the real type from the first bytes of the file. The file name extension must fit those bytes too. So x.html with GIF bytes does not pass. For types without a byte signature (like txt or csv), it uses the file name extension.
  • @Image() is @Mimes(['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'bmp']). No svg.
  • The JSON Schema of a file is {"type": "string", "format": "binary"}, plus the keys above.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
From dox_orm. Async: they run after all other checks passed.

Annotation Code Message @Unique(table, {column, ignoreParam, ignoreColumn, connection}) unique The {field} has already been taken @Exists(table, {column, connection}) exists The selected {field} is invalid
  • @Unique column default: the input key. @Exists column default: id.
  • ignoreParam: 'id' skips the row where ignoreColumn (default id) equals the path param {id}.
  • They add nothing to the JSON Schema.

See Database rules.

docs.title: Keys and DTO options
docs.text:
Annotation Does @Name('emailAddress') the input key for this field. Default: the field name in snake_case. @Dto() marks the class. @Dto(source: Source.query) where to read: Source.auto (default), Source.query, Source.body. @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) keys: KeyCase.snake (default) or KeyCase.field (the Dart name as is). @Dto(strict: true) unknown keys are errors. Default false: they are dropped. @Dto(messages: {...}) messages by code or key.code.

A /// doc comment on a field becomes its description in the JSON Schema.

docs.title: Types in detail
docs.text:
How each field type reads input. The short table is in Types.

  • JSON is strict. In a JSON body, "18" is not an int. You get the error integer.
  • Query and form data are text. Dox turns the text into the field type first. If it can not, you get the type error.
  • int takes 18 or 18.0, never a fraction. "4.5" or 4.5 gives integer.
  • bool in text takes true, 1, yes, on and false, 0, no, off (any case).
  • DateTime takes 2024-01-31 or 2024-01-31T10:00:00Z. A value without a time zone is read as UTC. The result is always UTC (isUtc == true). A number (timestamp) is not allowed.
  • An enum matches the Dart name exactly. "Admin" does not match Role.admin. Custom wire values (like "ADMIN") are not supported.
  • Object?, dynamic and Map<String, dynamic> take any value. They are not checked.
  • In query and form data, one value for a List<T> field gives a list with one item.
  • In bracket keys, list indexes are sorted and packed: items[3] alone gives a list with one item.
  • A list can have at most 1000 items, and keys can nest at most 10 levels. More gives 422.

docs.title: Body types
docs.text: Body Result application/json (or any +json type) read with strict JSON types application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data read as text, then converted any other content type 415 Unsupported Media Type JSON that is not valid 400 Bad Request JSON that is not an object (like [1, 2]) 422 with the key _root

docs.title: The order of checks
docs.text:
1. Read the input and convert types. Change text (@Trim, @Lowercase, @Uppercase). Find missing required fields.
  2. The field rules, top to bottom.
  3. The validate() method (nested DTOs first, then the parent).
  4. Async rules (@Unique, @Exists, your AsyncRule), one at a time, in field order.

Each step runs only when the step before it had no errors. So the database is never asked about input that is already wrong.

  • Steps 1 and 2 run per DTO. So one answer can have a type error in address and a rule error in items.1.
  • Inside one step, Dox collects the errors of all fields.
  • A default value is not checked by the field rules. Async rules check the final value.

docs.title: What the generator checks
docs.text:
The build stops with a clear error when:

  • a field is not final, or is not a parameter of the unnamed constructor,
  • a field type is not supported (see Types),
  • a rule does not fit the field type (like @Email() on an int),
  • a Maybe<T> field has no const Maybe.missing() default,
  • two @Dto classes in the app have the same name,
  • the class is generic, or extends another class (other than Object).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
This page shows how to check request input with typed DTO classes.

Write a class with @Dto(). Ask for it in your controller. Dox reads the request, checks it, and gives you a typed object. When the input is wrong, Dox answers 422 with the errors. Your controller does not run.

lib/app/http/dtos/create_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // nullable, so optional

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email, this.age});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart
class UserController {
  Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email;
    await user.save();
    return user;
  }
}

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
You do this once per app.

  1. Make a DTO with dox make:dto CreateUser. It writes lib/app/http/dtos/create_user.dto.dart.
  2. Run the generator: dox build_runner:build (or dox build_runner:watch). It writes a .dto.g.dart file next to each DTO, and one list of all DTOs in lib/dtos.g.dart.
  3. Give that list to the app:
lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:my_app/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos, // from lib/dtos.g.dart
  // ...
);

Dox uses no reflection, so it needs this list to find your DTOs. Without it, the server stops at start with a clear error.

docs.title: Use a DTO
docs.text:
Add a parameter with the DTO type. Dox checks the request before your method runs.

Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async { ... }

// with the request and a path param
Future<User> update(DoxRequest req, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }

Or check inside the method. req.validate<T>() returns the object, or throws the 422 error.

CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();

See Controller: parameters for the full rules.

docs.title: Required and optional
docs.text:
The Dart type decides. You do not write required or nullable.

Field Key missing Value null final String name; error required error required final int? age; null null final Role role; with this.role = Role.user Role.user error required
  • Rules on an optional field run only when it has a value.
  • A default value is used only when the key is missing. The rules do not check it.
  • An empty string counts as missing. So a required String rejects "". Add @AllowEmpty() to keep "".

docs.title: Missing or null? (for PATCH)
docs.text:
A T? field gives null for both. To know the difference, use Maybe<T>:

@Length(max: 500)
final Maybe<String?> bio; // default: const Maybe.missing()

// in the controller
if (body.bio.isPresent) {
  user.bio = body.bio.value; // can be null: the client cleared it
}

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Dart type JSON Query and form data String, int, double, num, bool the same JSON type text, converted DateTime an ISO 8601 string the same an enum the name, like "admin" the same RequestFile not allowed a file part a @Dto class an object bracket keys: address[city] List<T> an array tags=a&tags=b or tags[]=a Map<String, T> an object bracket keys: meta[color]

JSON is strict: "18" is not an int. Query and form data are text, so Dox converts them. Every detail is in Types in detail.

docs.title: Where the data comes from
docs.text:
Request Dox reads GET, HEAD, DELETE the query string POST, PUT, PATCH the body (JSON, form or multipart)

Dox reads one source. It never mixes the query and the body. To choose the source yourself:

@Dto(source: Source.query) // on the DTO
class SearchUsers { ... }

await req.validate<SearchUsers>(source: Source.query); // for one call

Path params are not part of a DTO. Ask for them as controller parameters, like int id.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
The input key is the field name in snake_case: firstName reads first_name.

final String firstName; // key: first_name

@Name('emailAddress')
final String email; // key: emailAddress
  • @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) uses the field names as they are.
  • Unknown keys are dropped. With @Dto(strict: true), an unknown key is an error.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Put rules on a field as annotations. They run from top to bottom. The first rule that fails gives the error.

@Trim()
@Lowercase()
@Email()
@MaxLength(255)
final String email;
Kind Annotations Text @Length, @MinLength, @MaxLength, @Email, @Url, @Uuid, @Ip, @Regex, @In, @NotIn, @StartsWith, @EndsWith, @Alpha, @AlphaNumeric, @AlphaDash Change text @Trim, @Lowercase, @Uppercase, @AllowEmpty Numbers @Min, @Max, @Range, @Positive, @GreaterThan, @LessThan, @In, @NotIn Lists @MinItems, @MaxItems, @UniqueItems Dates @After, @Before Files @MaxSize, @Mimes, @Image Database @Unique, @Exists

Every rule, with its error code and message, is in Validation rules.

  • A rule on a list checks each item: @Email() on a List<String>. Only the list rules check the list itself.
  • For a few allowed values, use a Dart enum, or @In(<String>['draft', 'published']).

docs.title: Nested objects and lists
docs.text:
A field can be another @Dto class, or a list of them.

@Dto()
class CreateOrder {
  final Address address;

  @MinItems(1)
  final List<OrderItem> items;

  const CreateOrder({required this.address, required this.items});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateOrder> schema = $CreateOrderDto;
}

Address and OrderItem are @Dto classes too. An error in a nested value has a path key, like items.1.quantity.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
A RequestFile field reads a file from multipart/form-data.

@Image()
@MaxSize('2MB')
final RequestFile avatar;

@Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])
final List<RequestFile> documents;

Dox checks the real file type from its first bytes. It does not trust the file name or the client. To save the file, see File upload.

docs.title: Checks across fields: validate()
docs.text:
Add a validate(DtoErrors errors) method to the DTO. Dox calls it after all field rules passed.

void validate(DtoErrors errors) {
  if (password != passwordConfirmation) {
    errors.add('password_confirmation', 'The passwords do not match');
  }
}
  • The key is the input key (snake_case). Use _root for an error about the whole body.
  • errors.has(key) tells you if a key already has an error.
  • The method can be async. Do not throw for bad input. Add an error.

docs.title: Database rules: @Unique and @Exists
docs.text:
These read the database, so they run last.

@Unique('users', column: 'email')
final String email;

@Exists('teams') // column defaults to id
final int teamId;

For an update, skip the row you are updating with ignoreParam:

// PUT /users/{id}
@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id')
final String email;

All options are in Validation rules: database. The full order of checks is in The order of checks.

docs.title: The error response
docs.text:
When a check fails, Dox answers 422 with one message per field:

{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email",
  "tags.0": "The tags may not be greater than 20 characters",
  "items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"
}

The key is the path to the value, with the input keys. List items use the index.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Change a message in one of these places. The first one wins.

  1. On the rule: @Email(message: 'Please check your email').
  2. On the DTO, by code or by key.code:
@Dto(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
  'integer': 'The {field} must be a number',
})
  1. For the whole app, with a MessageResolver. Use it for other languages:
class AppMessages extends MessageResolver {
  static const Map<String, Map<String, String>> _texts = <String, Map<String, String>>{
    'th': <String, String>{'required': 'กรุณากรอก {field}'},
  };

  @override
  String resolve(MessageRequest request) {
    String? template = _texts[request.locale]?[request.code]; // locale from Accept-Language
    if (template == null) {
      return super.resolve(request);
    }
    return format(template, request.params);
  }
}

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: AppMessages(),
  // ...
);

Placeholders: {field} (the last key), {value}, and rule values like {min} and {max}.

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
Extend Rule<T>. T is the field type (or the item type, for a list).

class Slug extends Rule<String> {
  const Slug({super.message});

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'slug'; // the error code
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be a slug';
  }

  @override
  bool check(String value, RuleContext context) {
    return _pattern.hasMatch(value);
  }

  static final RegExp _pattern = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$');
}

// use it
@Slug()
final String slug;
  • A rule with values: add final fields and override params. They become placeholders.
  • context.lookup('other.key') reads another input value.
  • A rule that needs the database: extend AsyncRule<T> and write checkAsync.

docs.title: Dynamic input
docs.text:
When the shape is known only at runtime (like form fields from the database), use a fluent schema:

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(fields));

See Fluent schemas. Use a DTO for everything else.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
A DTO is a normal Dart class. Make one directly to skip the checks:

CreateUser input = const CreateUser(name: 'Ann', email: 'ann@dox.dev');

To test the checks, use safeValidateMap. It never throws:

ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'A',
  'email': 'not-an-email',
});

expect(result.success, isFalse);
expect(result.errors['email'], 'The email is not a valid email');
  • validateMap does the same, but returns the object or throws.
  • source: Source.query reads the map like a query string. params: {'id': '5'} gives path params.
  • @Unique and @Exists need a test database.

docs.title: Build a blog API
docs.text:
This tutorial takes you from an empty folder to a small blog API that runs as one native binary. Every step has the full code and a curl command to check it.

The finished project is on GitHub: examples/blog-api. CI builds it and runs its tests on every push, so the code on these pages keeps working.

docs.title: What you will build
docs.text:
A JSON API for blog posts.

Method Path Who What it does GET /api/posts anyone list all posts GET /api/posts/{id} anyone one post, or 404 POST /api/posts logged in user make a post (201, or 422 on bad input) PUT /api/posts/{id} logged in user change a post POST /api/auth/register anyone make an account, get a token POST /api/auth/login anyone log in, get a token GET /api/auth/user logged in user the user of the token

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Dart 3.13 or newer: dart --version.
  • curl, to call the API.
  • About 15 minutes.

You do not need Docker or a database server. The app uses SQLite, which is one file in your project.

docs.title: The steps
docs.text:
1. Create the project
  2. Model and migration
  3. Routes and controller
  4. Validation
  5. Login with dox_auth
  6. Test
  7. Build and deploy

docs.title: The finished project
docs.text:
Files that you make or change in this tutorial are marked with *.

blog/
├── bin/
│   ├── migrate.dart              runs the dox migration:* commands
│   └── server.dart               runs the migrations, starts the server
├── db/migration/
│   ├── ..._create_posts_table.dart   *
│   ├── ..._create_users_table.dart
│   └── migrations.dart           the list of migrations (Dox writes it)
├── lib/
│   ├── app/http/controllers/
│   │   ├── auth.controller.dart  *
│   │   └── post.controller.dart  *
│   ├── app/http/dtos/
│   │   ├── login_user.dto.dart   *
│   │   ├── register_user.dto.dart *
│   │   └── save_post.dto.dart    *
│   ├── app/models/
│   │   ├── post/post.model.dart  *
│   │   └── user/user.model.dart
│   ├── config/
│   │   ├── app.dart              * adds the DTO list
│   │   ├── database.dart
│   │   └── env.dart              the .env keys, typed
│   ├── routes/api.dart           *
│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── auth_service.dart     *
│   │   └── orm_service.dart
│   ├── container.g.dart          * generated
│   └── dtos.g.dart               * generated
├── test/http_test.dart           *
├── .env                          *
├── Dockerfile
└── pubspec.yaml                  * adds dox_auth

Start with step 1: create the project.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the project
docs.text: This step makes a new Dox project, points it at SQLite, starts the dev server and calls the first route.

docs.title: 1. Install the CLI and make the project
docs.text:
dart pub global activate dox ^3.0.0-alpha
dox create blog
cd blog
dart pub get

dox create downloads the dox-sample template from GitHub and names the package blog. So every import in this tutorial starts with package:blog/.

Check the versions

Open pubspec.yaml. Every Dox package must be ^3.0.0-alpha. If the template has an older version, change it and run dart pub get again.

docs.title: 2. Use SQLite
docs.text:
dox create already made .env with a new random APP_KEY. The template already uses SQLite:

.env
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=<your new random key>

DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

Dox makes the file db/dox.sqlite at the first start. SQLite does not read the other DB_* lines. The app reads these keys through the typed class in lib/config/env.dart. See Environment variables.

The folder must exist

Dox makes the database file when it is missing, but not its folder. If you set DB_NAME=storage/blog.sqlite, run mkdir storage first.

docs.title: 3. Start the server
docs.text:
dox s

dox s runs the code generator and the server. It restarts the server when you save a .dart file. The first start is slower, because it compiles the SQLite library. The last line is:

Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)

Open it at http://localhost:3000. The number of isolates is the number of CPU cores.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
In a second terminal:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/ping

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
...

pong

The route is in lib/routes/api.dart. The ApiRouter has the prefix api, so /ping is served at /api/ping.

docs.text: Step 2: Model and migration

docs.title: Step 2: Model and migration
docs.text: This step makes the posts table with a Dart migration and a Post model for it.

docs.title: 1. Make the model and the migration
docs.text:
dox make:model Post -m

This makes two files and updates one:

File What it is lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart the model (new) db/migration/<date>_create_posts_table.dart the migration (new) db/migration/migrations.dart the list of all Dart migrations. Dox writes it. Do not edit it.

The template already has bin/migrate.dart. The dox migration:* commands run it.

docs.title: 2. Add the columns to the migration
docs.text:
Open the new file in db/migration. Add title and body:

db/migration/2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table.dart
// ignore_for_file: file_names
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreatePostsTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('posts', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('title');
      table.text('body');
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('posts');
  }
}
  • table.id() makes an auto increment primary key on every database.
  • table.timestamps() makes created_at and updated_at. The model fills them.

docs.title: 3. Add the fields to the model
4. Run the migrations on server start
docs.text:
Nothing to change here. The template's bin/server.dart already runs the migrations before the server starts:

bin/server.dart
import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);

  await Migrator(
    migrations: migrations,
    config: databaseConfig.getConnectionConfig(),
  ).migrate();

  await Dox().startServer();
}

This also works in the native binary of step 7.

docs.title: 5. Run the migration and the generator
docs.text:
dox migration:run

Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table

The model needs its generated file post.model.g.dart. dox s makes it while it runs. If dox s is not running, run the generator once:

dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

docs.text:
dox migration:status

Migration                             Batch  Status
2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table  1      Ran

docs.text: Step 3: Routes and controller

docs.title: Step 3: Routes and controller
docs.text: This step adds a resource controller and the routes to list, create and show posts.

docs.title: 1. Make the controller
docs.text:
dox make:controller Post -r

-r makes a resource controller with the seven CRUD methods. Replace the file with this. It keeps only index, store and show:

lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(DoxRequest req) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = req.input('title')
      ..body = req.input('body');
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}

How it works:

  • @Inject() puts the controller in the container. Dox makes it for you. dox s runs build_runner, which adds it to lib/container.g.dart. A new project already has container: registerContainer in lib/config/app.dart, so you change nothing there.
  • A controller returns a model or a list of models. Dox sends it as JSON.
  • response(post).statusCode(201) sets the status code.
  • show(int id) gets the {id} from the URL. /api/posts/abc answers 404, because abc is not an int.
  • req.input('title') reads the body as it is. It is not checked yet. Step 4 fixes that.

docs.title: 2. Add the routes
3. Start the server
docs.text:
dox s

If it is still running from step 1, it restarts by itself.

docs.text:
Make a post:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post."}'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}

List the posts:

[{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}]

Show one post:

{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}

docs.text: Step 4: Validation

docs.title: Step 4: Validation
docs.text: This step checks the input of create and update with a @Dto class. Bad input gets a 422 answer, and the controller does not run.

docs.title: 1. Make the DTO
docs.text:
dox make:dto SavePost

One class is enough for create and update, because both need the same fields. Replace the file with this:

lib/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'save_post.dto.g.dart';

/// Typed, checked input. Run `dox build_runner:build` after a change.
@Dto()
class SavePost {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 100)
  final String title;

  @Trim()
  @MinLength(10)
  final String body;

  const SavePost({required this.title, required this.body});

  static const DtoSchema<SavePost> schema = $SavePostDto;
}
  • A field that is not nullable and has no default is required.
  • The rules run from top to bottom. @Trim() removes spaces first. An empty string then counts as missing.
  • See Validation for all rules.

docs.title: 2. Give the DTO list to the app
docs.text:
The generator writes a list of all DTOs to lib/dtos.g.dart. Dox needs this list, because it does not use reflection. Add two lines to lib/config/app.dart:

lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:blog/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// DTOs (generated list in lib/dtos.g.dart)
  dtos: dtos,

  // ... the rest stays the same
);

docs.title: 3. Use the DTO in the controller
docs.text:
Ask for SavePost as a parameter. Dox checks the body and gives you a typed object. This also adds update, so PUT /api/posts/{id} works:

lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart
import 'package:blog/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(SavePost body) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    return _find(id);
  }

  /// PUT /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> update(int id, SavePost body) async {
    Post post = await _find(id);
    post
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return post;
  }

  Future<Post> _find(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}

Route.resource in lib/routes/api.dart sees the new update method and adds PUT and PATCH /api/posts/{id}. You change nothing there.

docs.title: 4. Run the generator
docs.text:
dox s runs it for you. Without dox s:

dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

It writes lib/app/http/dtos/save_post.dto.g.dart and lib/dtos.g.dart.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
A title that is too short, and a body that is too short:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hi","body":"Short"}'

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"title":"The title must be between 3 and 100 characters","body":"The body must be at least 10 characters"}

An empty body:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'

{"title":"The title is required","body":"The body is required"}

Good input still gives 201:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Second post","body":"Validation works now."}'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created

Update the first post:

curl -X PUT http://localhost:3000/api/posts/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hello Dox (edited)","body":"My first post, edited."}'

{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox (edited)","body":"My first post, edited.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:59:13.539886Z"}
