docs.text: Step 5: Login with dox_auth

docs.title: Step 5: Login with dox_auth
docs.text: This step adds register and login with a JWT token, and only lets a logged in user create or change posts.

docs.title: 1. Add the package
docs.text: dart pub add dox_auth:^3.0.0-alpha

docs.title: 2. Make the users table
docs.text:
The template already has a User model in lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart:

lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users', softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}

password is in hidden, so it is never in the JSON. This matters: the token holds the user as JSON, and anyone can read a JWT.

The users table already exists. The template has its migration, and the server ran it at the first start in step 1:

db/migration/2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table.dart
class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('name');
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.string('password');
      table.softDeletes();
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }
  // ...
}

table.softDeletes() makes the deleted_at column that softDelete: true needs. email is unique, so a second register with the same email fails.

docs.title: 3. Make the DTOs
docs.text:
dox make:dto RegisterUser
dox make:dto LoginUser
lib/app/http/dtos/register_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

part 'register_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class RegisterUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 2, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  const RegisterUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<RegisterUser> schema = $RegisterUserDto;
}

@Unique comes from dox_orm. It reads the database, so it runs after the other rules. dox_orm also has a class named Schema, so the import hides it.

lib/app/http/dtos/login_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'login_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class LoginUser {
  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  final String email;

  final String password;

  const LoginUser({required this.email, required this.password});

  static const DtoSchema<LoginUser> schema = $LoginUserDto;
}

docs.title: 4. Set up the auth service
docs.text:
A service runs once in every isolate at start. This one tells dox_auth which model to use and how to sign tokens:

lib/services/auth_service.dart
import 'package:blog/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/env.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Auth service
/// --------------------------
/// Sets up JWT login with the User model.
/// Tokens are signed with APP_KEY and last 7 days.
class AuthService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(
      AuthConfig(
        defaultGuard: 'api',
        guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
          'api': AuthGuard(
            driver: JwtAuthDriver(
              secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
              expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
            ),
            provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
          ),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}

Dox finds the service by itself. Run dart run build_runner build and it is in lib/container.g.dart. You do not add it to a list.

docs.title: 5. Write the auth controller
6. Protect the write routes
docs.text:
Replace Route.resource with single routes. The routes inside Route.middleware need a valid token:

lib/routes/api.dart
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get<ApiController>('/ping', (ApiController c) => c.pong);

    // Anyone can read posts.
    Route.get<PostController>('/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
    Route.get<PostController>('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.show);

    // Register and log in.
    Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/register', (AuthController c) => c.register);
    Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/login', (AuthController c) => c.login);

    // Only a logged in user can write posts.
    Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () {
      Route.get<AuthController>('/auth/user', (AuthController c) => c.user);
      Route.post<PostController>('/posts', (PostController c) => c.store);
      Route.put<PostController>('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.update);
    });
  }
}

AuthMiddleware reads the Authorization: Bearer <token> header and loads the user. When the token is missing or wrong, it answers 401 Authentication failed.

docs.title: 7. Migrate and generate
docs.text:
dox migration:run
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

dox s runs both for you when it restarts.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
Register:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}}

The same email again gives 422:

{"email":"The email has already been taken"}

A wrong password gives 401:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"wrong"}'

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Wrong email or password"}

Log in and keep the token in a shell variable:

TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}' \
  | sed -E 's/.*"token":"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
echo $TOKEN

A post without a token is refused:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}

With the token it works:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
...

{"id":3,"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token.","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z"}

Who am I:

curl http://localhost:3000/api/auth/user -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}

No password in the answer, because it is in hidden.

docs.text: Step 6: Test

docs.title: Step 6: Test
docs.text: This step writes one HTTP test for the list route and runs it.

docs.title: 1. Write the test
docs.text:
The template has test/http_test.dart. Replace it with this:

test/http_test.dart
import 'package:blog/config/app.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/database.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/testing.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() {
  late DoxTestClient client;

  setUpAll(() async {
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      config: databaseConfig.getConnectionConfig(),
    ).migrate();
    client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
  });

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await client.close();
  });

  test('GET /api/posts gives a list', () async {
    TestResponse res = await client.get('/api/posts');
    res.expectStatus(200).expectJson(isA<List<dynamic>>());
  });
}
  • DoxTestClient.start runs the app inside the test, on a free port. It does not clash with dox s.
  • It runs the migrations first, so the test also works on an empty database.
  • package:test is already in dev_dependencies of the template.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
dart test test/http_test.dart

00:01 +1: All tests passed!

Use another database for tests

The test uses the .env file, so it reads and writes db/dox.sqlite. To keep test data out of it, set another file for the test run: DB_NAME=test.sqlite dart test test/http_test.dart.

docs.text: Step 7: Build and deploy

docs.title: Step 7: Build and deploy
docs.text:
This step compiles the app to one native binary, runs it, and shows the Dockerfile of the project.

Never run production with dox s or dart run

They use the JIT compiler. It needs about 25 times more memory and starts slower. Build a native (AOT) binary for production.

docs.title: 1. Build the binary
docs.text:
dox build

Built with build_runner/aot in 1s; wrote 0 outputs.
Running build hooks...Running link hooks...
Generated: /.../blog/build/bundle/bin/server
[Dox] Built build/bundle. Run it with: cd build/bundle && ./bin/server

dox build runs the code generator, then dart build cli. The result is in build/bundle:

Path What it is bin/server the binary, about 10 MB. It needs no Dart SDK. lib/ native libraries from build hooks, like libsqlite3. Keep it next to bin/. db/ your migrations

docs.title: 2. Run the binary
docs.text:
The binary reads .env from the folder you start it in. Copy yours there, and make the db folder for the SQLite file:

cd build/bundle
cp ../../.env .env
mkdir -p db
./bin/server

Migrating: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrated: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)

The migrations run again, because db/dox.sqlite is a new file in build/bundle. The migration list is compiled into the binary, so no source code is needed. On a server you can skip .env and set real environment variables. They win over .env.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
In a second terminal:

curl http://localhost:3000/api/ping
curl http://localhost:3000/api/posts

pong
[]

The list is empty, because this is a new database file. Stop the server with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: 3. Docker
docs.text:
The project has a Dockerfile. It builds the same bundle and copies it to an empty (scratch) image:

Dockerfile
FROM dart:stable AS build

# Resolve dependencies first, so this layer is cached.
WORKDIR /app
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get

COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline
RUN dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

# `dart build cli` is AOT like `dart compile exe`, and it also runs
# build hooks. Native libraries go to build/bundle/lib.
RUN dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build

# Lay out the final file tree:
# /app/bin/server, /app/lib (native libraries), /app/db/migration,
# /app/storage and a writable /tmp (uploads bigger than 1 MB are
# streamed to a temp file).
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
  && cp -r db /out/app/db \
  # the native HTTP server (Rust) needs libgcc_s, which /runtime/ does not have
  && LIBGCC=$(find / -name libgcc_s.so.1 -path '*lib*' | head -n 1) \
  && mkdir -p /out$(dirname $LIBGCC) && cp $LIBGCC /out$LIBGCC

# Minimal serving image: the AOT runtime files from the dart image
# (`/runtime/`) plus our bundle. No Dart SDK, no source code.
FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app

# Config comes from env variables. The image has no .env file,
# so secrets stay out of it.
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]

Build and run it. The image has no .env file, so pass the config as environment variables:

docker build -t blog .
docker run -p 3000:3000 \
  -e APP_KEY=change-me \
  -e DB_CONNECTION=sqlite \
  -e DB_NAME=storage/blog.sqlite \
  blog

SQLite in Docker

The database file lives inside the container. It is lost when the container is removed. Mount a volume for it: -v blog-data:/app/storage. For a busy app, use Postgres or MySQL. See Database.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Deployment: HTTPS with a proxy, systemd, many machines.
  • Model: relationships and events.
  • Serializer: change the JSON shape of a response.
  • Authentication: all options of dox_auth.
  • OpenAPI: API docs from your routes and DTOs.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.5
docs.text:
• New timestamps option on @DoxModel. timestamps: false turns off created_at and updated_at, like $timestamps = false in Laravel. createdAt: null or updatedAt: null turns off one of them.
  • New primaryKeyType option on @DoxModel. Use primaryKeyType: String for a UUID key. The default is int.
  • Fix: IHttpException.toResponse() now returns {"code": errorCode, "message": message} for a text message, so the client gets the errorCode. A Map message is returned as it is.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
  • OpenAPI annotations, all optional: @Summary, @Description, @Tags, @Request, @Body, @Query, @Response, @ApiDeprecated, @ApiIgnore, @DoxController. Lower case names work too (@summary(...)), except @Response.
  • The DTO annotations (@Dto, @Length, @Email, ...) live in dox_validation. dox_core exports them.
  • IDoxRequest has no validate() and no processInputMapper() any more. Use a DTO.
  • Breaking (small): these names are exported by dox_core too. If a file also imports a package with a Request or Response class (like package:http) without a prefix, add a prefix to that import.
  • New @DoxEnv() and @EnvKey('X') for the typed env class.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.9
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.8
docs.text:
• Security: a JWT secret (SecretKey) shorter than 32 bytes stops the app with an ArgumentError when APP_ENV is not development, local or test. In those envs it prints one warning line. Make a key with dox key:generate or openssl rand -hex 32.
  • Hash now comes from dox_core. dox_auth had its own copy. package:dox_auth/src/hash.dart re-exports it. No change in behaviour. dox_auth now depends on dox_core.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.7
docs.text:
• Perf: attempt runs bcrypt in another isolate (Isolate.run). Before, each login blocked the server isolate for the whole hash.
  • Perf: the dummy hash for unknown users is made when the driver is created, in another isolate. Before, the first login paid for two hashes.
  • New: JwtAuthDriver(hashRounds: 10). Set it to the bcrypt cost of your stored hashes.
  • New: JwtAuthDriver(userCacheTtl: ...). Keeps the user of a token in memory for this time, so verifyToken does not run find(id) on every request. Off by default.
  • Security: JwtAuthDriver throws ArgumentError when the SecretKey is empty. Before, an app with no APP_KEY signed tokens with an empty key, so anyone could make a token for any user.
  • Security: attempt runs bcrypt also when no user is found, or when the user has no password. Before, an unknown email answered much faster than a wrong password, so the time told which emails have an account.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.6
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.5
docs.text:
• Breaking: JwtAuthDriver.expiresIn is 1 hour by default. Before, it was null, and tokens never expired.
  • New: named guards work. Use Auth(guard: 'admin') and AuthMiddleware(guard: 'admin'). Before, only defaultGuard was used.
  • A token keeps its guard name in the aud claim. A token from one guard does not work on another guard.
  • verifyToken checks the iss claim when issuer is set.
  • Breaking: AuthDriver methods get the guard name as a new parameter. AuthEngine().guard(name) replaces AuthEngine().driver and AuthEngine().provider.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.9
docs.text:
• New: lib/container.g.dart builder. It finds every @Inject() class, every class that extends Router, every class that implements DoxService and every @DoxModel in lib/. It writes registerContainer(IocContainer c), which makes each class with its constructor. Constructor parameters come from the container by type. Optional parameters that the container can not give keep their default. Required nullable ones get null.
  • The build stops with a clear message for a required parameter the container can not give, for a dependency cycle (it shows the chain, like A -> B -> A), and for an abstract or generic @Inject() class. Two classes with the same name work: every import has a prefix.
  • OpenAPI: typed routes (Route.get<C>(path, (C c) => c.method)) and Route.resource(path, ControllerClass) are read too.
  • Generates the query scopes: an extension with one method for each @Scope() method, and globalScopes for @Scope(global: true).
  • Generates the column casts: fromMap() and columnsToMap() use the cast of @Column(). bool and enum fields get a cast without cast.
  • Run dart run build_runner build to get the new code.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.8
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.7
docs.text:
• The generated fromMap() takes a DateTime from the driver as it is. It only parses a string.
  • New generated columnsToMap() with the columns only. convertToMap() adds the relations to it.
  • Models with no beforeGet hook get readsRowDates => true, so their rows skip the date to string step. A beforeGet hook still gets dates as strings.
  • tableColumns, preloadList, timestampsColumn and the relation matchers are const, so no new list or map is made on each call.
  • Run dart run build_runner build to get the new code.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.5
docs.text:
• @DoxModel(timestamps: false) makes a model without createdAt and updatedAt. createdAt: null or updatedAt: null turns off only one.
  • The primary key field has the type of @DoxModel(primaryKeyType: ...). It was always int?. The default is still int. The OpenAPI model schema uses the same type.
  • Fix: a preloaded relation with a two word name (like userInfo) was missing from toJson(). The generator looked for user_info in the preload list, but the list has userInfo.
  • Fix: the OpenAPI route scanner now puts one / between a group and a route path, like the router does.

docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
  • New builder dox_builder:openapi. It writes lib/openapi.g.dart with the OpenAPI docs of the app: it reads the Route.* calls, the controllers, the @Dto classes and the models. It writes nothing when the package has no controllers.
  • DtoJsonSchema, ModelSchema and JsonSchemaReader: the JSON Schema of a @Dto class, a model or any Dart type. Other builders can use them.
  • New: the DTO generator. For each @Dto class it writes $<Name>Dto (a const DtoSchema<Name>) into the .g.dart part: plain if checks per field, the converter, fromMap, toMap and the JSON Schema. It stops the build with a clear error for a bad DTO (a field that is not final, a type that is not supported, a rule that does not fit, a bad regex, ...).
  • New builder dox_builder:dtos. It writes lib/dtos.g.dart with every DTO of the app, for AppConfig(dtos: dtos). Two DTOs with the same name stop the build.
  • DtoReader: the one place that knows DTO keys. The OpenAPI docs use the same keys as the DTO (snake_case by default, @Name, @Dto(keyCase:)).
  • OpenAPI: @Regex (was @Pattern). @Format is removed. Form requests are removed.
  • Fix: the OpenAPI route list has the full path, with the Router prefix and Route.group() prefixes. Two '/' routes in two groups now each get their docs.
  • OpenAPI path params: every positional argument that is not the request and not a DTO.
  • New: @DoxEnv() classes get _$<Class> in the .g.dart part. Each getter is read from the env once, converted to its type (String, int, double, num, bool, Uri, Duration, enum, List) and kept in a final field. A getter body is the default. A nullable getter is optional. load() throws one EnvException with every missing or bad key.

docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.8
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.7
docs.text:
• Perf: the memory driver removes expired items and expired locks in a sweep after many writes. Before, a key that was written once with a ttl and never read again stayed in memory forever.
  • Perf: the memory driver with no max_size does not reorder the map on every hit. The order is only needed for LRU.
  • Perf: a tagged cache reads all tag versions with one many call (one MGET on Redis). tags(...).flush() raises all tag versions at the same time. Before, each tag was one round trip after the other.
  • Perf: the Redis driver frees a lock with EVALSHA. It sends the full script only when Redis does not know it yet.
  • Perf: the file driver makes the cache folder only when it is missing. Before, it ran create(recursive: true) on every write. Lock tokens use one shared Random.secure().

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.6
docs.text:
• New CacheManager.close(). It closes the connections of every store that was built. The Redis driver closes its connection and its pool connections, with no reconnect. Memory, file and null stores do nothing. It is safe to call twice. A store used after it is built again.
  • New CacheDriver.close(), for one driver. Custom drivers can override it. The default does nothing.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.5
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.4
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.3
docs.text:
• New: getRaw(key) gives the stored value as JSON text, with no decode. Use it to send a cached value as a JSON response. Memory and Redis return the stored text as is. A stored String comes back with its quotes ("bar"). The stored format did not change, so old values still read the same.
  • Faster get: a plain store builds the key with no async step. itemKey now returns FutureOr<String>. Memory get costs about 0.6 µs instead of 0.86 µs. Memory getRaw costs about 0.3 µs.
  • New Redis option pool_size: the most connections one store opens (ioredis maxConnection). Default is 10, the same as before.
  • Uses ioredis 2.0.0-alpha.2. It sends all commands on one shared connection and writes them together (auto-pipelining). A Redis read costs much less CPU. The cache now uses one connection per store, so pool_size rarely matters.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.1
docs.text:
• Uses ioredis 2. Redis error replies throw RedisError.
  • Redis: no value size limit by default (was 60 KB). maxValueBytes is still there if you want one.
  • Redis: many uses one MGET, putMany uses one pipeline, flush uses SCAN + DEL (no Lua).
  • First release.
  • CacheManager with named stores and custom drivers.
  • Drivers: memory (with LRU), file, Redis, null.
  • remember, pull, add, increment, many, tags and atomic locks.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• make:* is now the main name of every generator: make:controller, make:middleware, make:dto, make:serializer and make:model, like make:migration, make:factory and make:seeder. The create:* names still work as aliases.
  • New dox make:job <name>: makes lib/app/jobs/<name>.job.dart and bin/queue.dart when it is missing. It prints a hint to add dox_queue and to run build_runner.
  • New dox queue:work, queue:failed, queue:retry, queue:forget and queue:flush: run bin/queue.dart with the same flags.
  • New dox schedule:work, schedule:run, schedule:list and schedule:test <name>: run bin/schedule.dart.
  • These commands pass the terminal through, send SIGINT and SIGTERM to the app script so a worker can stop by itself, and return its exit code. When the script is missing they print how to set it up.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.9
docs.text:
• dox make:controller (create:controller) writes @Inject() above the class, and no global controller instance. The file shows the typed route to use. The command says to run build_runner.
  • New dox make:factory <model>: makes db/factories/<model>.factory.dart.
  • New dox make:seeder <name>: makes db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart, writes the seeder list db/seeders/seeders.dart and makes bin/seed.dart when it is missing.
  • New dox db:seed [--class=<name>]: runs bin/seed.dart. The default seeder is DatabaseSeeder.
  • New dox migration:fresh (or migrate:fresh): drops all tables, then runs all migrations.
  • --seed after migration:run, migration:refresh or migration:fresh runs the seeders when the migrations end well.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.8
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.7
docs.text:
• Breaking: create:controller no longer takes -ws. Dox uses Socket.IO for realtime now. See the Socket.IO docs for a namespace class.
  • Security: dox create now copies .env.example to .env and writes a new random APP_KEY. Before, every new app used the same public key from the template. You no longer run cp .env.example .env.
  • The .env.example of the CLI has an empty APP_KEY. Run dox key:generate to set one.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.6
docs.text:
• Fix: dox key:generate dropped .env lines with more than one = (like DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?sslmode=require). It also dropped comment lines. Now it only changes the APP_KEY line. Every other line stays as it is.
  • Fix: dox create crashed with Failed to decode data using encoding 'utf-8' when the template had a binary file (for example db/dox.sqlite-shm). It now skips files that are not UTF-8 text. It only writes a file when its content changes.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.5
docs.text:
• Fix: dox create my_app without --version crashed with a RangeError.
  • Fix: dox create picked the GitHub "latest" template release, which skips pre-releases. During the 3.x alpha that gave the old 2.x template. It now takes the newest template with the same major version as the CLI.
  • Fix: dox env:generate read KEY=3000 # note as text, not as an int. A # after a space is now a comment.
  • Fix: dox update ran a plain dart pub global activate dox, which skips pre-releases. During the 3.x alpha it installed the old 2.x CLI. It now installs the newest version with the same major version as the CLI, from the pub.dev version list.

docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• Fix: dox build no longer passes --delete-conflicting-outputs to build_runner (it was removed and printed a warning).
  • Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
  • dox build now runs dart build cli (AOT, with build hooks). The output is build/bundle/. Start it with cd build/bundle && ./bin/server.
  • New dox create:dto <name>: makes lib/app/http/dtos/<name>.dto.dart. dox create:request is removed.
  • dox create:controller -r uses int id for the resource methods.
  • New dox openapi:generate [dir]. It runs the app's bin/openapi.dart and writes openapi.json and openapi.yaml (default storage/openapi).
  • New dox env:generate: makes lib/config/env.dart (the typed env class) from .env.example.
  • New dox env:check: loads the typed env and prints every missing or bad key (exit code 1).

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.1
docs.text:
• Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
  • Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
  • See the release notes for all main changes.
  • Generated models import package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.9
docs.text:
• New: a real IoC container. IocContainer (Dox().ioc) has get<T>(), has<T>(), singleton<T>(), factory<T>(), instance<T>(), override<T>() and clearOverrides(). Each isolate has its own container: a singleton is one instance per isolate, made on first use.
  • New: AppConfig(container: registerContainer) with the function from lib/container.g.dart (made by dox_builder). Every isolate runs it. The routers and services it finds are registered for you, so AppConfig.routers and AppConfig.services can stay empty. The ones you list there still work and come first.
  • New: typed routes. Route.get<UserController>('users', (UserController c) => c.index) (also post, put, patch, delete and the others). The controller comes from the container, once per isolate, at start. (UserController c) => c.index without <UserController> works too. Route.resource('users', UserController) takes a controller class.
  • New: a controller parameter whose type is in the container gets it from the container.
  • New: route model binding for @DoxModel classes. A controller parameter of type User gets the User of the {user} param (or the next param), found by its primary key. No row answers 404. Route.bind still wins.
  • Breaking: the old IocContainer methods register, registerByName, registerSingleton and getByName are removed. Use factory, singleton and get.
  • New: named routes. Route.get('/users/{id}', c).name('users.show'), then route('users.show', params: {'id': 5}) gives /users/5. query: adds a query string. Route.group(..., name: 'admin.') puts a prefix in front of the names inside. Resource routes are named blogs.index ... blogs.destroy; Route.resource(..., name:) picks another base name. A name used twice stops the app at start. An unknown name, a missing param or an extra param throws an ArgumentError.
  • New: route model binding without dart:mirrors. Route.bind<User>('user', (String id) => User().find(id)) runs before the controller of every route with a {user} param. The controller gets it as a User user parameter, or with req.bound<User>('user'). A binder that gives null answers 404.
  • New: ExceptionHandler, the one place that turns an error into a response. Extend it and set AppConfig(exceptionHandler: ...). report(error, stackTrace) logs, render(error, req) picks the response. The default answers are the same as before. A URL with no route goes through it too.
  • Breaking: AppConfig.errorHandler and defaultErrorHandler are removed. Override ExceptionHandler.report instead. It gets the same errors: every error that is not an IHttpException, also errors outside a request. A thrown value that is not an Exception or Error (like a String) is now reported too.
  • responseHandler still works and still runs after render.
  • New: RateLimit middleware. RateLimit(max: 60, per: Duration(minutes: 1), key: (DoxRequest req) => req.ip()). One request too many gets 429 with Retry-After. Every answer has X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining. The counts live in Redis when the default cache store is Redis (shared by all isolates and servers), else in memory. Fixed window. New TooManyRequestsException.
  • New: SecurityHeaders middleware. It adds X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, and Strict-Transport-Security on https requests only. Each one can be changed or turned off with null. Content-Security-Policy is off by default.
  • New: Route.health('/health', checks: {...}). It answers 200 {"status": "ok"}, or 503 when a check throws, returns false or times out. HealthCheck.cache() checks the cache. The error text is in the answer only in development and local.
  • New: package:dox_core/testing.dart with DoxTestClient. DoxTestClient.start(appConfig) runs the app in the test on a free port. get, post, put, patch, delete, send, withHeaders and withToken. TestResponse has status, body, json, headers and expectStatus, expectJson, expectBody, expectHeader.
  • dox_core now depends on matcher (for the expect methods of TestResponse).

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.8
docs.text:
• Uses dox_http_native 3.0.0-alpha.8: pipelined requests are about 2.8 times faster (1 core: 172k to 480k req/s). Normal requests are as fast as before.
  • Security: every file response (File, Storage().stream(), Storage().download(), Route.files) sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Before, a File response and a raw download did not.
  • New: Route.files(path, download: true) sends every file as a download (Content-Disposition: attachment). Use it for user uploads. html, svg, xml and javascript files are still always sent as a download in a sandbox.
  • Fix: a trusted proxy X-Forwarded-For hop with a port (1.2.3.4:5678, [::1]:5678) is now read without the port. Before, it was not a valid ip, so req.ip() could be wrong. A bare IPv6 like ::1 still works.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.7
docs.text:
• Breaking: dox_websocket is gone. Use dox_socketio for realtime. Dox().websocket and Dox().setWebsocket() are removed.
  • Breaking: Route.websocket(path, handler) is now a raw WebSocket route. handler gets the open WebSocket and the DoxRequest. Middleware runs first. A request that is not a WebSocket upgrade gets 400.
  • dox_http_native now lives in its own repo (dartondox/dox-http-native). Dox uses it from pub.dev (^3.0.0-alpha.7). Its build hook downloads a ready-built library, so you do not need Rust.
  • Perf: faster route matching. A plain route is found with one map lookup, also when a param route was added before it (as long as that param route can not match the same path). Param routes are grouped by their first path segment, so a request only tries the routes that can match. The first matching route still wins.
  • Perf: the request handler reads Host and Content-Type once per request. Host is read only when the app has a Route.domain() route. HttpBody.read() takes an optional contentType.
  • Perf: on the native server, a JSON or form body is used as it is, with no stream in between. The size limit is still checked.
  • Perf: JSON responses are encoded in 8 KB chunks, not 256 bytes.
  • Perf: fewer objects per request. RouteData.params, DoxRequest.param and DoxRequest.method are made on first use. RouteData.domainLower is made once. CORS header lists are joined once.
  • Perf: one Future less per async request (then(onError:) instead of then().onError()).
  • Perf: multipart parsing makes its regexes once, and no longer builds a Future.any per chunk.
  • Perf: LogMiddleware lowercases the redact words once, not per key.
  • Perf: an error response reads APP_ENV and lowercases it only when the value changed.
  • Perf: IocContainer calls T.toString() once per call.
  • Breaking: the dart:io server is gone. Every app runs on the native server (dox_http_native), also an app with WebSocket or Socket.IO routes. AppConfig.server, the ServerBackend enum and the DOX_SERVER env var are removed. DoxServer.usesNative() and the isolateId option of DoxServer.listen() are removed.
  • Breaking: when the native library does not load, Dox stops at start with an error. It says why (eg. an ABI mismatch) and how to fix it (install Rust so the build hook can build it, or rebuild your lib_path library). Before, Dox logged a warning and used dart:io.
  • On a graceful stop (SIGTERM, Dox().stop()), open WebSockets get close code 1001.
  • Perf: AESEncryptor keeps the key bytes of the last secret and writes the output into one buffer. Decode reads the nonce and text without copies. The output format is the same.
  • New: Hash.makeAsync() and Hash.verifyAsync(). They run bcrypt in another isolate, so a request does not block the server.
  • New: Hash.rounds (default 10) sets the bcrypt cost. Hash.make() also takes rounds:.
  • Security: the app does not start when APP_KEY is empty, not exactly 32 characters, or one of the old public sample keys from .env.example. With such a key anyone can sign tokens and cookies. In APP_ENV development, local or test Dox only logs a warning. A longer key (eg. 48 or 64 characters) is refused too, because AES needs a key of 16, 24 or 32 bytes and every encrypted cookie failed with it. Before, only an empty key in production stopped the app. Run dox key:generate for a new key.
  • Security: a multipart part header with many backslashes (name="\\\\...) no longer blocks a server isolate for hours (ReDoS in the quoted string regex).
  • Security: a StreamFile response (Storage().stream(), Route.files()) with an html, xml, svg or javascript type is sent with Content-Disposition: attachment and Content-Security-Policy: sandbox. Every StreamFile gets X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Before, an uploaded x.html or x.svg was shown inline, and its script ran on the app origin (stored XSS).
  • Security: a Route.domain() route only matches when the Host header matches. Before, a request with no Host matched every domain route. A Host with a port (admin.app.com:8080) now matches Route.domain('admin.app.com').
  • Security: an encrypted cookie is bound to its name (AES-GCM associated data). A value made for locale gives null when it is sent as user_id. AESEncryptor.encode()/decode() take a new associatedData option. Encrypted cookies made by older versions no longer decrypt, so req.cookie() gives null for them once. Users may need to log in again.
  • Security: DoxCookie is HttpOnly by default. secure is null by default, which sets Secure when the request came over https (req.scheme(), see trustedProxies). Set httpOnly: false or secure: false to change it.
  • Security: the native server checks maxBodySize and maxMultipartSize on their own. Before, Rust let any body up to the bigger limit (100 MB) through, so a JSON body could take 100 MB of RAM before Dart said 413.
  • New AppConfig.bodyTimeout (default 120 seconds). On the native server, a client that does not send the whole body in this time gets 408. It stops slow clients that hold memory and connections.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.6
docs.text:
• Security: Storage().putRequestFile() and RequestFile.store() no longer trust the client file name when the bytes are a known format that does not match it. Before, a valid png sent as a.html passed @Image/@Mimes and was saved as .html, so Route.files() served it as text/html on the app origin (stored XSS). Now it is saved with the extension of the bytes (.png).
  • Security: new upload file names use a random uuid (v4), not a time-based one (v1). A v1 name shows the upload time and the server, and the next name is easy to guess.
  • Security: trustedProxies: ['*'] trusts the direct peer only. req.ip() is the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop, the one the proxy added. Before, * also trusted every hop in the header, so req.ip() was the left-most value, which the client sets (X-Forwarded-For: 6.6.6.6). That broke IP rate limits and allow lists, also behind the Fly.io proxy of the deploy guide.
  • Security: LogMiddleware writes [REDACTED] for body fields and headers whose name has password, passwd, secret, token, authorization, cookie, api_key, api-key or apikey in it (upper or lower case). Before, the login body (with the password) and, with withHeader: true, the Authorization header went to the log as plain text. Change the list with LogMiddleware(redact: [...]).
  • Security: an error that is not an IHttpException answers 500 with {"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}. The error text is sent only when APP_ENV is development or local. Before, the client always got error.toString(), which can hold SQL, table names, file paths or database hosts. errorHandler still gets the full error.
  • Graceful shutdown closes the cache stores of Cache() (eg. Redis), in every isolate, after the DoxShutdown services. Your app needs no extra code.
  • The ORMService of a new project implements DoxShutdown and calls SqlQueryBuilder.close(), so the database connections close on shutdown too. In an older project, add this to lib/services/orm_service.dart: 
    class ORMService implements DoxService, DoxShutdown {
  // setup() as before

  @override
  Future<void> shutdown() async {
    await SqlQueryBuilder.close();
  }
}

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.5
docs.text:
• Fix: CORS origin can be a list. Dox compares the request Origin with the list and sends back only the origin that matches, or no header. Before, it joined the list with commas, and browsers rejected it. A list also sends Vary: Origin.
  • Breaking: AESEncryptor now uses AES-GCM with a random nonce for each message. Before, it used AES-CTR with an all-zero nonce and no message check. Old encrypted cookies and values can not be read.
  • Breaking: AESEncryptor.decode throws DecryptException (400) when the text was changed or the key is wrong. Before, it printed an error and returned ''.
  • req.cookie() returns null for an encrypted cookie that can not be decrypted.
  • Fix: Hash.verify returns false for a malformed hash. Before, it threw.
  • AESEncryptor and DecryptException are now exported from package:dox_core/dox_core.dart.
  • Fix: in .env, KEY=value # note gave the value value # note. A # after a space now starts a comment. A # inside quotes, or with no space before it, is kept.
  • Fix: the .env parser removed every quote character inside a value. Now only the quotes around the value are removed.
  • Fix: HEAD requests got 404, also HEAD /docs. A HEAD request now runs the GET route of the same path. The answer has the status and headers of GET, with no body.
  • New: Dox listens on PORT when APP_PORT is not set. Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set PORT. APP_PORT still wins.
  • New: AppConfig.host and the env var APP_HOST pick the network interface to listen on, like 127.0.0.1. The default is the same as before: all interfaces (::, IPv6 and IPv4).
  • Fix: the start log always said http://127.0.0.1:<port>. It now shows the real host and port, like http://[::]:3000.
  • Removed the unused sprintf dependency.
  • New: graceful shutdown. On SIGTERM or SIGINT every isolate stops taking new connections and lets open requests finish, up to AppConfig.shutdownTimeout (default 8 seconds). Then Dox runs DoxShutdown services and exits with code 0. Before, open requests were cut. A second signal stops at once.
  • New: DoxShutdown. A service that also implements it gets shutdown() in every isolate on stop, to close connections.
  • New: await Dox().stop() stops the server gracefully in every isolate, without exit.
  • Fix: an s3 storage disk without bucket, key or secret failed with Null is not a subtype of String. Now it fails with a clear message that names the missing setting.
  • Fix: a URL with no route now answers like a thrown NotFoundHttpException. The body is JSON ({"code": "not_found", "message": "GET /x not found"}), and the app responseHandler runs for it, so apps can format it.
  • Fix: the error answer of an IHttpException now has its errorCode. A text message gives {"code": "<errorCode>", "message": "<text>"} as JSON. Before, the body was plain text and errorCode was never sent. A Map message (like validation errors) is still sent as it is.
  • Fix: the Logger now reads LoggerConfig.level. Lines below that level are not printed. Levels from low to high: debug, info (and success), warn, error (and danger).
  • Fix: Route.group('blogs') with Route.get('all') made /blogsall. Path parts now join with one /. This also works for nested groups, Route.prefix and Route.resource.
  • Fix: Route.resource hid every error from the controller. Now it only skips methods the controller does not have.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.4
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.3
docs.text:
• New: Cache().getRaw(key) gives the cached value as JSON text, with no decode. Send it as a JSON response with no extra encode step.
  • New Redis cache option pool_size (see dox_cache).

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• New default server: dox_http_native (Rust hyper parses HTTP, your code stays in Dart). Hello world goes from about 41k to about 144k req/s on one isolate. Set server: ServerBackend.dartIo in AppConfig (or DOX_SERVER=dartio) to use dart:io. Dox uses dart:io by itself, with one warning line, when the native library does not load, and for apps with WebSocket or Socket.IO routes.
  • Faster requests: a simple GET hello world went from about 31k to about 40k req/s on one isolate (plain dart:io is about 46k). A request with no body and sync middleware and controller now runs with no Future. req.ip(), the query, req.all() and cookies are read on first use only. Reading the client ip was the biggest cost, because it asks the socket. Clean paths skip the two regex calls, and plain routes are found with a map lookup.
  • Fix: a @Dto body with a RequestFile field shows as multipart/form-data in the OpenAPI docs.
  • Fix: req.ip() gave ::ffff:127.0.0.1 for IPv4 clients. Now it gives 127.0.0.1. The same goes for X-Forwarded-For hops.
  • Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
  • Removed the encrypt package (not maintained, and it blocked pointycastle 4). AES for cookies and the file cache now uses pointycastle 4. The output is the same, so old cookies and cache files still decode.
  • Fix: Env.get() of a missing key with no default gave the text "null". A missing APP_KEY became the key "null", which anyone can guess. Now String gives '', String? gives null, and int/num/double/bool throw a clear error. New: Env.get<bool>().
  • Startup stops with an error when APP_KEY is empty and APP_ENV=production. Other environments log a warning.
  • New: typed input with DTOs. A controller asks for a @Dto class by type: store(CreateUser body). Dox reads the body (or the query for GET), checks it, and answers 422 with {"items.1.quantity": "..."} when it is wrong. await req.validate<T>() does the same inside a method. See the Validation guide.
  • New: AppConfig(dtos: dtos) (from lib/dtos.g.dart) and AppConfig(validationMessages:) for other languages. req.locale is the first Accept-Language.
  • New: typed controller parameters. DoxRequest anywhere, one @Dto, and String, int, double, num, bool path params by position. A path param that does not fit its type answers 404. The types are read once at start; an unknown type stops the server with a clear error.
  • New: optional path params {id?}.
  • New: query strings and form data with repeated keys (tags=a&tags=b) and bracket keys (address[city], items[0][name]) for DTOs.
  • A DTO answers 400 for a body that is not valid JSON, and 415 for a body type it can not read.
  • RequestFile implements FileInput and keeps its first bytes, so @Mimes and @Image check the real file type.
  • Breaking: removed req.validate(Map), req.validateAsync(), FormRequest, AppConfig(formRequests:), DoxValidator, IocContainer.registerRequest() and processInputMapper(). Use a DTO. req.validateSchema(schema) stays for input you only know at runtime.
  • Breaking: a controller with more path params than the route has {...} params stops the start. Before, the extra ones got ''.
  • Fix: a typed path param like int id gave a 500 (it was always a String).
  • A ValidationException from dox_validation (for example schema.parse() in a controller) answers 422.
  • dox_core exports dox_validation (not its ValidationException), with the DTO annotations. dox_orm also has Schema, and package:uuid has Uuid: use hide or a prefix in a file that needs both.
  • Breaking: Cache() runs on dox_cache. AppConfig.cache is a dox_cache CacheConfig(defaultStore:, stores:) with option maps. CacheDriverInterface and FileCacheDriver are removed. Values must be JSON types. put without a duration keeps the value forever (was 1 hour). New: add, pull, increment, decrement, remember, rememberForever, lock, tags.
  • Breaking: Storage() runs on dox_storage. AppConfig.fileStorage is now AppConfig.storage (StorageConfig(defaultDisk:, disks:) with option maps for local, s3, memory). StorageDriverInterface and LocalStorageDriver are removed. An unknown disk name throws.
  • Storage().stream() and download() stream from any disk (S3 too), with Content-Length. New: url, signedUrl, use() for the full Disk.
  • New Route.files('files') serves local signed URLs (403 for a bad signature). New catch-all route param {path*}.
  • OpenAPI: AppConfig(openApi: OpenApiConfig(...)) adds /docs, /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml. On by default only when APP_ENV is development or local. Bodies come from the route body: option or a DTO. Dox().writeOpenApi(dir) writes the files.
  • RouteData.preMiddleware now holds the group and router middleware.
  • Socket.IO: AppConfig(socketIo: SocketIoConfig(enabled: true, ...)) serves /socket.io/ on the app port, before the router. Route.mount(prefix, handler) is the raw hook. Off by default.
  • No extra work per request when OpenAPI or Socket.IO is off.
  • OpenAPI docs are automatic. dart run build_runner build writes lib/openapi.g.dart. Pass it as OpenApiConfig(registry: openApiRegistry). Each route then gets its summary and description (from the /// comment), tags, Class.method operation id, typed path params, request (a @Dto class) and answer schema (from the return type), plus 401, 404, 422 and 500.
  • A middleware whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware adds bearerAuth to the docs, with no config.
  • A GET or DELETE request class becomes query params in the docs.
  • dox_core exports OpenApi, OpenApiRegistry, OpenApiOperation, OpenApiRouteBinding and ResponseDoc of dox_openapi.
  • The OpenAPI JSON and YAML are encoded once and kept, not on each request.
  • New EnvReader and EnvException for the typed env class (@DoxEnv()). The real environment wins over .env, the same as Env.get(). Env.get() stays for dynamic keys.
  • OpenAPI: /docs uses Scalar by default. OpenApiConfig(ui: DocsUi.swagger) gives Swagger UI. New OpenApiConfig options: scalar: ScalarOptions(...) (theme, dark mode, download button, proxy) and pageTitle.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.1
docs.text:
• Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
  • Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
  • See the release notes for all main changes.
  • Faster: streamed bodies, all CPU cores, faster router.
  • uuid 4 and mime 2.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.9
docs.text:
• New Seeder and SeederRunner. A seeder puts data in the database. call() runs other seeders. SeederRunner(seeders: seeders).run(args) runs DatabaseSeeder, or another one with --class=<name>, in one transaction. It reads the database from .env, the same as the migrations.
  • New Migrator.fresh() and the fresh command of Migrator.run(). It drops every table of the database, then runs all migrations.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.8
docs.text: • A migration that runs inside a transaction you already opened (eg. with Migrator(connection: ...)) now uses a savepoint. A failed migration undoes only its own work.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.7
docs.text:
• Breaking: migrations run on the dox_orm drivers: the native Postgres and MySQL drivers, and SQLite. The postgres and mysql_dart packages are gone. When the native library does not load, the migration stops with an error that says why.
  • Breaking: Migrator(connection: ...) takes a dox_orm DBDriver now, eg. SqlQueryBuilder().dbDriver. The migrator does not close it. New Migrator(config: ...) takes a ConnectionConfig, eg. databaseConfig.getConnectionConfig(), and closes it at the end.
  • TLS works the same as dox_orm. For Postgres, sslmode=require encrypts and verify-full also checks the certificate. For MySQL the certificate is checked. Add verifyCertificate=false to DATABASE_URL to skip the MySQL check in development.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.6
docs.text: • A DB_HOST that starts with / is a MySQL Unix socket file too (Postgres: the socket folder). ?socket=/path works in a mysql:// DATABASE_URL.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.5
docs.text:
• DATABASE_URL support. When it is set, it wins over DB_CONNECTION and the other DB_* keys. Its sslmode (Postgres) or ssl (MySQL) option turns TLS on.
  • A DB_HOST that starts with / is a Postgres Unix socket folder, like /cloudsql/project:region:instance on Cloud Run.
  • Migrations read real environment variables too. Before, a .env file hid them. Now a real env var wins over .env, the same as Env.get() of dox_core. An empty value, or null, counts as missing.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.4
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.3
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
  • sqlite3 3 (SQLite is bundled, no system library needed).

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.1
docs.text:
• Removed the dox_migration executable from pubspec (its script was removed before). Use the dox CLI.
  • Added SQLite: DB_CONNECTION=sqlite and DB_DATABASE=<file path>.
  • MySQL driver is now mysql_dart (was mysql1). The MySQL 8 default login (caching_sha2_password) works.
  • migrate() and the other commands also take a pool (postgres Pool, mysql MySQLConnectionPool). Each file runs in one transaction on one connection.
  • Breaking: a passed mysql connection must be a mysql_dart MySQLConnection or MySQLConnectionPool (not mysql1).
  • Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.

• Support MySQL. Set DB_CONNECTION=mysql in .env (default is postgres)
  • Run each statement of a .sql migration one by one, inside a transaction
  • Rollback undoes only the last batch, newest first. Add step, reset() and refresh()
  • Stop at the first failed migration
  • Fix .sql parsing: a - in the sql no longer cuts the up or down part
  • Fix statement split: ; inside quotes, comments or $$ bodies does not split

docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• A request body with a file field (format: binary, also in a list) uses multipart/form-data instead of application/json, so the /docs page can send files. RouteDoc(bodyMediaType:) sets it by hand.
  • Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
  • DoxRouteAdapter reads preMiddleware and body from a route when it has them.
  • A Dox catch-all param {path*} and an optional param {id?} become {path} and {id} in the document.
  • OpenApiOperation.formRequest is removed (form requests are gone).
  • New OpenApiRegistry, OpenApiOperation and OpenApiRouteBinding: the docs that dox_builder finds in the code. OpenApiRegistry.find() matches them to a live route.
  • RouteDoc and ApiDoc.route() take deprecated.
  • OpenApiServer builds and encodes the document once, on the first call, and keeps it. Make a new OpenApiServer after you change the OpenApi.
  • OpenApi.yamlEmitter is now a public field.
  • /docs uses Scalar (@scalar/api-reference 1.75.1) by default. OpenApiServer(ui: DocsUi.swagger) gives Swagger UI. ScalarOptions sets the theme, dark mode, download button and proxy (off by default). The title and the config are escaped.
  • Swagger UI updated to 5.34.0.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.1
docs.text:
• First release.
  • Build an OpenAPI 3.1 document with OpenApi and ApiDoc.
  • Add undocumented Dox routes with DoxRouteAdapter.
  • Output as JSON and YAML, write files, serve /openapi.json, /openapi.yaml and /docs.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.9
docs.text:
• Breaking: the ModelObserver methods now have the same names as the model hooks: onSaving, onSaved, onCreating, onCreated, onUpdating, onUpdated, onDeleting, onDeleted, onRestoring, onRestored, onForceDeleting and onForceDeleted. Rename the methods in your observers, for example created(User user) to onCreated(User user).
  • New model factories: import 'package:dox_orm/factory.dart';. Extend Factory<User> and write definition(). Then use count(n), state(), sequence(), has(), make(), makeOne(), create() and createOne(). See the Factories docs page.
  • New query scopes. @Scope() on a static model method adds it as a query method, like User().isActive().get(). @Scope(global: true) adds it to every query of the model. Remove it with withoutGlobalScope('name') or withoutGlobalScopes().
  • New attribute casts with @Column(cast: ...): JsonCast, ListCast<E>, BoolCast, EnumCast<E> (by name or by index), or your own Cast<T> class. bool fields get BoolCast and enum fields get EnumCast without cast.
  • New withCount('posts'), withSum('posts', 'views') and withMax('posts', 'views'). They add the value with a subquery, for hasOne, hasMany and manyToMany relations. Read it with countOf('posts') or aggregate('posts_sum_views'). toJson() has it too.
  • all() now uses the where conditions of the query, like get(). Before, it used only the soft delete check.
  • New: package:dox_orm/testing.dart with refreshDatabase(). Use setUp(refreshDatabase) in tests: it empties every table and starts the ids at 1 again, on Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite. The migrations table keeps its rows. keep: keeps more tables.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.8
docs.text:
• A transaction() inside another transaction now uses a savepoint (SAVEPOINT sp_N). When the inner function throws, only its work is undone, and the error is thrown again. If the caller catches the error, the outer transaction goes on and can commit. Before, the inner one joined the outer one, so an inner error always undid the outer work too. Works on Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite. New DBDriver.savepoint().
  • Postgres: new extra['sslRootCert'], the path of a PEM file with the CA certificates to trust for verify-full. sslrootcert in DATABASE_URL sets it. New ConnectionConfig.postgresSslRootCert. Needs the next dox_postgres_native release.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.7
docs.text:
• Breaking: Postgres and MySQL use only the native drivers. The Dart drivers (postgres and mysql_dart packages) are gone. So are PostgresDriver, MysqlDriver, DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart and extra['native'].
  • Breaking: when the native library does not load, createDriver() and SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig() throw an UnsupportedError. It says why the library did not load and how to fix it. Before, the ORM used the Dart driver and printed a warning.
  • Postgres has TLS now. useSSL: true is mode require (no certificate check, like libpq). extra['sslMode'] is a String: disable, prefer, require or verify-full. sslmode in DATABASE_URL sets it. prefer and allow in the url now mean "TLS when the server has it".
  • Breaking: errors are PgServerException and PgException for Postgres, and MysqlException for MySQL. dox_orm exports them. The ServerException classes of the postgres package and MySQLServerException are gone.
  • Breaking: ConnectionConfig loses getDatabaseConnection(), postgresEndpoint, mysqlHost, mysqlPort, mysqlAllowPublicKeyRetrieval and mysqlAcceptBadCertificate. postgresSslMode is now a String. The collation, timeoutMs, timeZone (MySQL), serverPublicKey, allowPublicKeyRetrieval and the postgres package pool keys of extra are no longer read.
  • Breaking: getDatabaseDriver() and SqlQueryBuilder.initialize() take a PgNativePool for Postgres and a MysqlNativePool for MySQL.
  • On Postgres, a List in insert() or update() is sent as json text, so it fits a json column. New DBDriver.columnValue().
  • dox_postgres_native and dox_mysql_native now live in their own repos (dartondox/dox-postgres-native, dartondox/dox-mysql-native). Dox uses them from pub.dev (^3.0.0-alpha.7). Their build hooks download ready-built libraries, so you do not need Rust.
  • Faster belongsTo load. It reads each owner once with WHERE owner.id IN (...), with no join to the children. Before, a user with 10,000 blogs came back 10,000 times. Children of the same owner now get the same model object.
  • save() on a new model runs one INSERT and reads the id from it. There is no SELECT after it. insert() and create() use RETURNING * on Postgres and SQLite, so they also skip the SELECT. MySQL still reads the row with find().
  • save() on an existing model sends only the columns that changed since the last load or save. A Map or List field is always sent. When nothing changed, save() runs no query and updated_at stays as it is. Before, it always ran an UPDATE with every column that had a value.
  • Fix: after restore(), a save() on the same model sent the old deleted_at again and deleted the row again. Now deleted_at is not sent, because it did not change.
  • LIMIT and OFFSET are bound parameters (@dox_limit, @dox_offset). Every page gives the same SQL, so the drivers reuse one prepared statement.
  • On Postgres, whereIn and whereNotIn with only int or only String values send one array parameter (= ANY(@p), <> ALL(@p)). A list of any size gives the same SQL. Other lists keep one parameter per value.
  • Relations of one model (preload and eager) load at the same time outside a transaction, so the native drivers send them in one batch. Inside a transaction they still load one by one. New DBDriver.inTransaction.
  • Rows of a model made by the new generator skip the date to string step. fromMap() takes the DateTime of the driver as it is. toMap(original: true) still gives dates as ISO strings.
  • New Model.columnsToMap(): the columns only, without relations. save() uses it, so it no longer turns preloaded relations into JSON.
  • Less work per row: the where, join and order lists of a model are made only when used. getPreload() and the generated getters do not make a new list or map on each call.
  • The SQL text is no longer scanned for double spaces on each query. orderBy() without a direction no longer adds a space.
  • QueryBuilderHelper.runQuery() no longer has the clean parameter.
  • Fix: in a native Postgres or MySQL transaction(), when the rollback after an error also fails, the first error is thrown. Before, the rollback error replaced it.
  • The native Postgres driver shares one pool for all isolates with the same settings, like the native MySQL driver. maxConnectionCount is for the whole process on both native drivers.
  • The Dart Postgres driver keeps its prepared statements after a session command like SET, SHOW, BEGIN or COMMIT. Before, any query that was not select/insert/update/delete dropped all of them.
  • Breaking: column and table names in select, where, orderBy, groupBy, join, insert and update must be plain names (name, table.name, table.*, *, name as alias). Anything else, like count(*), throws an ArgumentError. Before, a name with ( went into the SQL as it is, so user input could add SQL. Use selectRaw, whereRaw or the new orderByRaw and groupByRaw for expressions.
  • Breaking: the operator of where() and join() must be one of =, !=, <>, <, >, <=, >=, like, not like, ilike (any case). Any other value throws an ArgumentError.
  • New fillable and guarded lists on Model. When set, create(), insert() and update() on the model drop the keys that are not allowed, so User().create(req.body) can not set is_admin. insertMultiple() on the model drops them from each row too. Both are empty by default, so nothing changes until you set them.
  • Breaking: TLS checks the server certificate. Postgres useSSL (and sslmode=verify-ca or verify-full in a url) now uses SslMode.verifyFull. sslmode=require in a url stays SslMode.require like libpq: it encrypts but does not check the certificate (eg. Heroku). The Dart MySQL driver no longer accepts a bad certificate. Set extra['verifyCertificate'] to false (or ?verifyCertificate=false in a url) to skip the check for a self-signed certificate in development.
  • Breaking: the Dart MySQL driver no longer asks the server for its RSA key by default. It still asks with TLS on, or on localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 and a Unix socket. Give the key in serverPublicKey, or set allowPublicKeyRetrieval: true.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.6
docs.text:
• MySQL and MariaDB Unix sockets. A host that starts with / is the socket file, like /var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock or /cloudsql/project:region:instance on Cloud Run. Works on the native and the Dart driver. In a url, use ?socket=/path or ?host=/path.
  • New SqlQueryBuilder.close(). It closes every open database connection of the isolate: the default and all named connections, on every driver (native Postgres and MySQL, the Dart drivers and SQLite). It is safe to call twice. Call it on shutdown, eg. from a DoxShutdown service.
  • New DBDriver.close(), for one driver. Custom drivers can override it. The default does nothing.
  • SqlQueryBuilder().dbDriver throws a StateError with a clear message when the ORM is not set up (or after close()).
  • After close(), the native MySQL driver throws a StateError on a new query or transaction. Before, the query still ran when another isolate kept the shared pool open.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.5
docs.text:
• DATABASE_URL support. ConnectionConfig.fromUrl() reads postgres://, postgresql://, mysql://, mariadb://, sqlite: and file: urls: url-decoded user and password, host, port, database, sslmode and other options (they go to extra).
  • DatabaseConfig has a new url. It is DATABASE_URL from the environment when not given. When it is set, it wins: it replaces the default connection. Pass url: '' to turn it off.
  • Postgres Unix sockets. A host that starts with / is a socket folder, like /cloudsql/project:region:instance on Cloud Run. Works on the native and the Dart driver. Use ?host=/cloudsql/... in a url.
  • Breaking: the finders are typed. On a model, get() and all() give Future<List<T>>, find() and getFirst() give Future<T?>, and paginate() gives Future<Pagination<T>> (page.data is a List<T>). QueryBuilder.table() gives maps: get() is Future<List<Map<String, dynamic>>> and getFirst() is Future<Map<String, dynamic>?>. QueryBuilder.table() has no type argument and no second argument any more.
  • Breaking: groupBy() and rawQuery() rows are maps, so use them on QueryBuilder.table(). On a model, get() throws a StateError for them. count() with groupBy() still works on a model.
  • Breaking: the default foreign keys use the model name, like Laravel. A User model with table: 'users' gives user_id, not users_id. The default pivot table of @ManyToMany also uses the model names (artist_song). Keys you set yourself work as before. New Model.foreignKeyName gives the default key of a model.
  • Breaking: save() inserts when the model is new and updates when the row is in the table (model.exists). Before, it updated when the primary key was set. So a new model with a key you set yourself, like a UUID, is now inserted.
  • QueryBuilder.query() has a new connection parameter, to run a raw query on a named connection.
  • Fix: withConnection() did not reach save(), delete(), forceDelete() and restore(). They used the default connection. Now they use the connection of the model. Models that a query returns keep the connection of the query, and relation queries use the connection of the parent model. Model.withConnection() returns the model, so Blog()..withConnection('other') works.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.4
docs.text: • Version bump only, to match the other packages.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.3
docs.text:
• Postgres and MySQL/MariaDB now use the native drivers by default (dox_postgres_native and dox_mysql_native). You do not change any config. If the native library does not load, the ORM uses the Dart driver and prints one warning line. Set DOX_DB_DRIVER=dart, or extra: {'native': false} on one connection, to use the Dart driver. driverFactory still wins over all of this.
  • Breaking: PostgresNativeDriver and MysqlNativeDriver moved into dox_orm. Import them from package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart.
  • PostgresNativeDriver.query does one less async step per query.
  • Faster queries on all databases. Each connection keeps its prepared statements (LRU, 100 by default, extra['preparedStatementCacheSize']). The same query now has the same sql text, so the statements are reused. find() no longer sends LIMIT 1 OFFSET 0: LIMIT and OFFSET are only sent when set, and never OFFSET 0. Less work per row when models are built. A find by id on SQLite went from 23 µs to 6 µs.
  • Less Dart work per query. A plain find() builds its SQL once per driver, table and column, and reuses it. A model makes its maps and lists only when they are used. Rows become models without one more await when there is nothing to preload. ORM work per World().find(id) went from 2.6 µs to 1.0 µs (no database, AOT).
  • New ConnectionConfig.driverFactory: plug in your own driver class with one line. The default and the named connections use it.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
  • sqlite3 3. SQLite is now bundled by a build hook, so no system libsqlite3 is needed.
  • Breaking: dart compile exe does not work with build hooks. Use dart build cli (or dox build).
  • SQLite: set busy_timeout before journal_mode = WAL. Before, many isolates that opened the same file at start could fail with "database is locked".
  • New DTO rules @Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id') and @Exists('teams'). They run after all other checks. A List field is checked with one WHERE IN query. Soft-deleted rows count too.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.1
docs.text:
• Renamed from dox_query_builder to dox_orm. Change package:dox_query_builder/dox_query_builder.dart to package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart. The old package still works for now: it only re-exports this one.
  • Added SQLite (Driver.sqlite, package sqlite3). database is a file path or :memory:. Uses WAL, busy_timeout and foreign keys. One connection per isolate. See the docs for limits.
  • MySQL driver is now mysql_dart (was mysql1). The MySQL 8 default login (caching_sha2_password) works. It uses a real connection pool (maxConnectionCount, default 10), prepared statements with bound values, and one pooled connection per transaction.
  • Breaking: extra['characterSet'] (a mysql1 type) is no longer read. Use extra['collation'] (default utf8mb4_general_ci). getDatabaseConnection() for MySQL now returns a MySQLConnectionPool.
  • Breaking: MySQL TIME columns are now a String (was a Duration). BLOB columns are Uint8List (was text).
  • ConnectionConfig: user, password and port are optional (not used by SQLite).
  • Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
  • Added whereNull, whereNotNull, orWhereNull, orWhereNotNull, whereNotIn, orWhereIn, orWhereNotIn and selectRaw.
  • Added QueryBuilder.transaction(). Postgres now uses a real connection pool (maxConnectionCount) and no longer runs each query in its own transaction.
  • Added boolean() schema column (Postgres BOOLEAN, MySQL TINYINT(1), read as bool).
  • Table and column names are now quoted ("name" on Postgres, `name` on MySQL). On Postgres, quoted names are case sensitive. Use selectRaw/whereRaw for raw SQL.
  • count() ignores limit, offset and orderBy. With groupBy it now returns the number of groups (before: the size of the first group).
  • save() can set a field to null on update.
  • insert() works with any primary key type (uuid strings too).
  • model.delete() and model.forceDelete() only delete that record. Before, they had no where condition.
  • forceDelete() also deletes soft deleted rows. withTrash(false) on a model without soft deletes no longer adds a deleted_at filter.
  • hasOne, hasMany and manyToMany work with a custom localKey.
  • insertMultiple() uses keys from all rows. Missing keys use the column default.
  • MySQL: only JSON columns are decoded (arrays too). MariaDB keeps decoding JSON-like text, because it stores JSON as text.
  • Schema: unique() on a column that is already unique is skipped. Default values are escaped.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.7
docs.text:
• Uses ioredis 2.0.0-alpha.3, which can send and get binary messages. RedisAdapter and SocketIoEmitter take ioredis clients.
  • RedisAdapter reads msgpack and JSON messages. Before, it read only JSON, so the Socket.IO emitters (Node.js, PHP, Python, Go) did not work. They use msgpack.
  • Breaking: RedisAdapter writes msgpack by default, like @socket.io/redis-adapter. Use format: RedisFormat.json for Node.js servers with a JSON parser.
  • Fix: binary data in JSON Redis messages is written as a Node.js Buffer ({"type":"Buffer","data":[...]}). Before, it was written as a plain list of numbers.
  • RedisAdapter handles the requests on socket.io-request#<nsp>#: socketsJoin, socketsLeave and disconnectSockets from emitters and other servers. It answers fetchSockets, allRooms and broadcasts with acks from Node.js servers, so they do not wait for a timeout.
  • New SocketIoEmitter(redis): sends events, socketsJoin, socketsLeave and disconnectSockets through Redis without a Socket.IO server. Same format as @socket.io/redis-emitter.
  • New MsgPack encoder and decoder.
  • Performance: a broadcast builds the websocket text frame and its UTF-8 bytes once and shares them with every client (new SharedText). Before, each client built and encoded its own copy.
  • Performance: a broadcast with no except and at most one room goes over the room members directly. Before, it copied all socket ids into new sets each time.
  • Breaking: SocketIoServer.listen() starts a native server (dox_http_native), not a dart:io one. The websocket transport uses the native WebSocket upgrade. Long-polling works the same. attach() still takes any HttpServer, also a dart:io one.
  • Security: on the native server, a websocket message over maxHttpBufferSize bytes is closed with 1009 in Rust, before Dart reads it.
  • Security: a binary packet nested deeper than 32 levels is a parse error (SocketDecoder(maxDepth: ...)). Before, a deep packet overflowed the stack and could stop the server. Any decode error now closes only that one connection.
  • Security: many CONNECT packets for one namespace at once make only one socket. Before, each one made a socket that stayed in memory.
  • Security: websocket compression is off. A small compressed message could grow very big in memory.
  • Security: when CorsOptions.origins lists origins, a websocket from another origin gets 403. With no cors, or with *, any origin is still allowed.
  • Breaking: CorsOptions(origins: ['*'], credentials: true) throws an ArgumentError. Before, it sent back any origin with credentials.
  • Security: a middleware error that is not a SocketIoException sends {"message": "Internal error"} to the client and writes the real error to stderr.

  • Security: a client whose CONNECT is refused is closed after connectTimeout. Before, it could stay connected forever.

  • Security: a binary packet may have at most 10 attachments (SocketDecoder(maxAttachments: ...)). More closes the connection with a parse error. Before, a client could send 51000000-[...] before any auth and the server kept every binary frame after it in memory.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.7
docs.text:
• Perf: object, list, map and union schemas work out isAsync once and keep the answer. Before, the whole schema tree was walked on every validateSchema call.
  • url() now allows only http and https links. Pass schemes to allow others.
  • File type checks now also need the file name extension to fit the bytes. A .html file with GIF bytes no longer passes @Image. Only another known type (like .png with GIF bytes) or a type the browser runs (html, htm, xhtml, svg, xml, js, mjs) is refused. A file with no or an unknown extension (like a canvas upload named blob) passes when the bytes match.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• A JSON body that is not an object now says The request body must be a JSON object. (key _root). Change it with the message key _root.object.
  • Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
  • New: DTOs. A class with @Dto() and rule annotations (@Length, @Email, @Min, @Regex, @MaxSize, ...). dox_builder writes a const DtoSchema<T> with the checks, a converter and the JSON Schema. See the Validation guide.
  • New: DtoSchema<T> with validateMap, safeValidateMap, fromMap, toMap and toJsonSchema. It is also a Schema<T>.
  • New: Maybe<T> knows a missing key from null. DtoErrors for checks across fields in validate().
  • New: FileTypes finds the real type of a file from its first bytes. @Image() and v.file().image() do not allow svg.
  • New: MessageRequest.locale, ParseState.params. A message set on a rule is used as it is; the resolver only fills its placeholders.
  • Rule has a const constructor and a final message, so a rule class works as an annotation. AsyncRule.failedItems() checks a list in one call.
  • FileInput has length and head (the first bytes).
  • Schema has a const constructor. The fluent schemas extend BaseSchema.
  • Text length messages say "characters".
  • Breaking: removed v.fromRules(), v.registerRule(), RuleRegistry, RuleDefinition, CallbackRule and all rule strings. Use a DTO, or a Rule<T> class.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.1
docs.text:
• First release of dox_validation.
  • Fluent schema builder: string, int, num, bool, date, enum, literal, list, object, map, union, any, file.
  • optional, nullable, nullish, defaultTo, transform, refine, superRefine, async refinements.
  • Coercion with v.coerce for query strings and form data.
  • parse, safeParse, parseAsync, safeParseAsync with issue paths.
  • Standard Schema interface (StandardSchema).
  • JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 / OpenAPI 3.1) export with toJsonSchema().
  • Custom Rule classes and a global MessageResolver.
  • Laravel style string rules with v.fromRules().
